lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 2 (It's good for you!) — ish joyida sog'lom turmush, yo'l ko'rsatish iboralari
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 5–6.5: Student's Book, Unit 2, 20–21-betlar (Listening Section 2, CD1 Track 5–6); Workbook, Unit 2, 14-bet (Listening Section 2, Track 3).
objectives: Section 2 da (bitta so'zlovchi, ijtimoiy mavzu) MCQ va xarita birga kelganda tayyorlanish vaqtini bo'lish: MCQ kalit g'oyasi + xaritani oldindan "o'qish".
MCQ da variantdagi so'z eshitilgani uchun emas, savoldagi SHARTga mos kelgani uchun tanlash ("most important", "main advantage").
Xaritada boshlang'ich nuqta, kompas va mo'ljallarni (roundabout, main entrance, reception) tinglashdan oldin topish.
Yo'nalish iboralarini tez tushunish: opposite, beyond, just before, behind, directly in front of, on the right-hand corner.
Xarita tuzoqlarini tanish: so'zlovchi bir joyni tilga oladi, keyin boshqasiga yo'naltiradi ("not this one, but...").
materials: Student's Book, Unit 2, 20–21-betlar — savollar va xarita sahifasi (quyida rasm), CD1 Track 5–6 audiosi.
Workbook, Unit 2, 14-bet — savollar va konferensiya binosi rejasi, Track 3 audiosi (imtihon rejimi).

Recording script rasmlari — darsda faqat ustozda; tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqariladi. Uy vazifasi uchun ustoz darsdan keyin guruhga SB Track 6 va WB Track 3 audiolarini hamda SB skript rasmini yuboradi; WB skript rasmi faqat diktant topshirish muddati tugagach yuboriladi (aks holda qolganlar diktantni skriptdan ko'chiradi).
Kolonka yoki quloqchin; audio platformadan ochiladi (internetni oldindan tekshiring).
Doskada Jony Academy mashqi uchun ferma xaritasi (pastdagi jadvaldan chiziladi) va yo'nalish iboralari ro'yxati.
timeline: Kirish
SB 1-mashq: "Kim sog'lomroq yashaydi — siz yoki sherigingiz?" When did you last...? How often do you...? — juftlikda 3 daqiqa.
Section 2 kombinatsiyasi
Ustoz doskada: tayyorlanish vaqtini bo'lish, MCQ shart so'zlari, xaritani o'qish tartibi, yo'nalish iboralari, tuzoqlar.
Sinf mashqi
Yo'nalish iboralari va "savoldagi shart" mashqi (og'zaki).
Student's Book: Track 5–6
30 soniya → Track 5 (Q1–5) → xarita bilan 30 soniya → Track 6 (Q6–10) → javoblar izoh bilan.
Workbook: Track 3
Imtihon rejimi: 1-mashq (qachon gapiryapti?), tayyorlanish, audio bir marta, 10 savol.
Jony Academy mashqi
Ustoz "Hillside Organic Farm" skriptini o'qiydi: 5 MCQ + 5 xarita; bir marta, keyin tekshiruv.
Tahlil va skript
Xato savollar skriptda topiladi; tuzoq gaplar belgilanadi; xatolar daftari.
Xulosa va vazifa
Uyga: shadowing, diktant va o'z xaritangiz bo'yicha ovozli yo'l ko'rsatish.

intro: Section 2 — bitta so'zlovchi ijtimoiy mavzuda gapiradi: gid, rahbar, tashkilotchi. U ko'pincha ikki qismga bo'linadi: birinchisida umumiy ma'lumot (MCQ), ikkinchisida joylar yoki bino rejasi (map / plan labelling). 6.0 darajasida aynan shu juftlik eng ko'p uchraydi.

Tayyorlanish vaqtini ikkiga bo'ling. MCQ uchun: savolning SHART so'zini tagiga chizing — "why", "recommends", "most important", "advice", "asks the nurses to". Xarita uchun: qayerdan boshlanadi (main building, main entrance, reception), kompas qayerda, qanday mo'ljallar bor (roundabout, Tye Road, trees, main hall).

MCQ: uch variantning hammasi odatda eshitiladi, lekin so'zlovchi "the main advantage" yoki "the most important thing" deb faqat bittasini ajratadi. Javob paraphrase bilan keladi: "I've made a lot of new friends there" = "it's a good way to meet people". SB Track 5 dagi isbot gaplarini tinglashdan oldin aytmang — ular javoblar tekshiruvida ko'rsatiladi.

Xarita: savollar tartibi = audio tartibi. So'zlovchi sizni xarita bo'ylab "yetaklaydi": har yo'nalishdan keyin qalam bilan joyingizni belgilang. Bitta joyni yo'qotsangiz, keyingi savolda ko'rsatilgan mo'ljaldan ("go back to the main building") qayta boshlang.

Yo'nalish iboralari: opposite (qarshisida), beyond / past (o'tib), just before (sal oldin), behind (orqasida), directly in front of you (to'g'ri oldingizda), on the right-hand corner (o'ng burchakda), the second turning on the left (chapdagi ikkinchi burilish).
Chap va o'ng — yurayotgan odamniki. Agar siz xaritada pastga (janubga) qarab yursangiz, sizning chapingiz xaritada o'ngda bo'ladi. Shuning uchun kompas bo'yicha o'ylash ("to the east") xavfsizroq.
Tuzoq: so'zlovchi bir joyni aytib, keyin boshqasiga yo'naltiradi ("there's a snack bar by the entrance, but I'd recommend the restaurant by the lake"). Oxirgi yo'naltirilgan joy — javob.
formulas: tilga olinib rad etilgan → tuzoq; "but" yoki "most" dan keyingisi → javob
out of the front → turn left → past the library → on your right
presentation: MCQ va xarita orasida vaqt bo'ladimi?
Ha, odatda qisqa pauza. Shu paytda xaritani qayta ko'zdan kechiring va start nuqtasiga barmog'ingizni qo'ying.
Xaritada harflar ko'p, javoblar kam. Nega?
Ortiqcha harflar — tuzoq. SB da 8 ta harf (A–H), 5 ta savol: 3 ta harf ishlatilmaydi.
"Left" deyildi, lekin xaritada o'ngga ketyapman.
Yurayotgan odamning chapi. Qaysi tomonga qarab yurayotganingizni tekshiring yoki kompasga tayaning.
Bitta joyni o'tkazib yubordim. Nima qilaman?
Taxminiy harf yozing va keyingisiga o'ting. Har yangi joy ko'pincha asosiy binodan qayta boshlanadi.
Bitta harf ikki marta javob bo'lishi mumkinmi?
Map labellingda odatda yo'q. Agar ikki savolga bir harf chiqsa, bittasini qayta tekshiring.
MCQ da variantdagi so'z aynan eshitildi. Demak shumi?
Ko'pincha aksincha — aynan eshitilgan so'z tuzoq bo'ladi. G'oyani tekshiring: variant savoldagi shartga mos kelyaptimi?
notes: 5.0 da MCQ va map labelling alohida o'rganilgan. Endi ular bitta Section 2 da ketma-ket: o'tish paytida xaritaga qarashga vaqt topish — asosiy ko'nikma.
Tekshiruvda xaritani ekranga chiqaring va skript bo'yicha yo'lni qalam bilan chizing. O'quvchilar har burilishda "qayerdamiz?" deb aytib boradi.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: WB Track 3 dan keyin xaritadagi ortiqcha xonalardan (E, G) biriga o'zlari yo'l ko'rsatib gapirsin.
mistakes: Gym tilga olinadi, lekin tavsiya emas

how: CORE — sog'lom turmush va ish joyi so'zlari; STRONG — konferensiya va tashkilot so'zlari; SUPER — yo'l ko'rsatish va nutqdagi iboralar.
Har o'quvchi akademiyadan eng yaqin bekat, do'kon yoki parkgacha bo'lgan yo'lni 4–5 gap bilan tushuntiradi (uy manzili emas), kamida 3 ta yo'nalish iborasini ishlatib.
core: A balanced diet includes fruit and vegetables.
Muvozanatli ovqatlanishga meva va sabzavot kiradi.
Our supervisor showed us around the hospital.
Hygiene is very important in a hospital.
Germs can live on a desk for days.
Mikroblar stol ustida bir necha kun yashashi mumkin.
Shift work makes regular meals difficult.
The canteen is open until eight.
Take a short break every two hours.
Har ikki soatda qisqa tanaffus qiling.
The staff recreation centre has a small library.
Xodimlar dam olish markazida kichik kutubxona bor.
She takes a vitamin supplement in winter.
strong: The company started a cycling initiative.
Please complete the questionnaire before the conference.
Stress in the workplace is a common problem.
Ish joyidagi stress — keng tarqalgan muammo.
The pharmacy is opposite the bank.
The pool is just beyond the trees.
super: Don't fall into the fast-food trap.
We took your answers into account.
It's called Healthy Kitchen — the name speaks for itself.
U "Healthy Kitchen" deb ataladi — nomi o'zi aytib turibdi.
Make the most of the free sessions.

class_ex.title: Yo'nalish iboralari
class_ex.instr: Ustoz iborani o'qiydi, o'quvchilar o'zbekcha ma'nosini aytadi va doskadagi oddiy chizmada qo'li bilan ko'rsatadi.
items: directly opposite you
just beyond the line of trees
go past the turning for Tye Road
the second turning on the left
directly behind the main building
on the right-hand corner
just before you reach the roundabout
why: "Opposite" — ko'chaning yoki yo'lakning narigi tomonida, yuzma-yuz.
"Beyond" = narigi tomonida. Daraxtlar oldida emas — ulardan keyin.
"Go past" — burilmasdan o'tib ketish. Ko'p o'quvchi shu joyda buriladi — tuzoq.
Birinchi burilishni sanamang — ikkinchisi kerak.
"Behind" — asosiy kirishga nisbatan orqa tomonda (SB da back exit).
Chorraha yoki burilishdagi o'ng burchak.
"Just before" — hali yetmagan, sal oldinda.
class_ex.note: Doskaga oddiy chizma: bitta asosiy bino, bitta aylanma yo'l, bitta ko'cha va daraxtlar. Har iborada bitta o'quvchi chizmaga borib, joyni ko'rsatadi.

class_ex.title: Savoldagi shart: qaysi biri?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar savolga javob beradi va qolgan ikki narsa nega javob emasligini aytadi.
items: "Swimming is good for your heart, and it helps with back pain, but what I like most is that it clears my head." — Main benefit for the speaker?
"You could buy a bike or join a club, but honestly, just getting off the bus one stop early is enough." — What does the speaker recommend?
"There's a café on the ground floor, but it's expensive. The staff kitchen upstairs is free and has a microwave." — Where should staff eat?
"We tried running sessions, then cooking classes. What people asked for most, though, was advice on sleep." — What was most requested?
answers: getting off the bus one stop early
why: "What I like most" — asosiy foyda. Yurak va bel — tuzoq.
"You could ... but honestly ... is enough" — "but" dan keyingi qism tavsiya.
Kafe tilga olinadi, lekin "expensive" — so'zlovchi boshqasini tavsiya qiladi.
"What people asked for most" = most requested. Birinchi ikkitasi — sinab ko'rilgan narsalar.
class_ex.note: SB Track 5 dagi 2- va 4-savol aynan shu tuzilishda: avval bir narsa aytiladi, "but" dan keyin javob.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 5: Debbie's talk to new nurses (Q1–5)
intro: Kasalxona rahbari Debbie Green yangi hamshiralarga ovqatlanish, jismoniy faollik, xavfsizlik va gigiyena haqida gapiradi. Tinglashdan oldin 30 soniya: har savolning shart so'zini tagiga chizing (why, recommends, most important, advice, asks).
Savollar sahifasi va xarita quyida rasm sifatida (Q6–10 xaritasi Track 6 uchun).

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Variantdagi so'zni emas, g'oyani tinglang. Uchala variant ham tilga olinishi mumkin.
items: 1 According to Debbie, why do some people fail to eat a balanced diet? A) They don't know how to cook. B) They don't have enough time to cook. C) They don't feel hungry enough to cook.
2 Debbie recommends that staff should keep fit by A) using a gym. B) taking up a new sport. C) changing some daily activities.
3 Which benefit of exercise does Debbie think is most important? A) It helps you sleep. B) It keeps your heart healthy. C) It improves mental skills.
4 What advice does Debbie give the nurses about health and safety? A) to avoid drinking coffee B) to use the canteen at night C) to take regular breaks
5 When she talks about hygiene, Debbie asks the nurses to A) wash their hands regularly. B) keep away from germs. C) help with the cleaning.
why: "It's often too easy to grab something quick, because you're tired or busy". Tuzoq: C — "when you feel hungry" eshitiladi, lekin ochlik yetishmasligi haqida emas.
"It may just be a question of doing things differently" — liftda emas, zinada. Tuzoq: A — "may not have time to join a gym"; B — "rather than starting a very active sport".
"You'll find that you don't lie awake at night ... and that's the main advantage of exercise". Tuzoq: B — yurak tilga olinadi, lekin "main advantage" emas.
"You shouldn't work for more than three hours without a break". Tuzoq: A va B — "that cup of tea or coffee in the canteen" faqat misol.

"Make sure that you don't leave even a small amount of rubbish around ... there are brooms in the cupboards, so use them". Tuzoq: A — qo'l yuvishni allaqachon bilishadi ("trained to clean your hands"); B — mikroblar tilga olinadi.
tasks.note: Kalit: 1B 2C 3A 4C 5C — har javobning isbot gapi va tuzog'i izohda berilgan. 5-savolda ko'p o'quvchi A ni tanlaydi — "hands" so'zi birinchi eshitiladi.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 6: Map of the hospital (Q6–10)
intro: Tinglashdan oldin xaritada toping: MAIN BUILDING (start), BACK EXIT, aylanma yo'l, TYE ROAD, daraxtlar va kompas. Debbie har safar asosiy binodan boshlaydi.
SB 4-mashq: juftlikda bitta harfni tanlab, sherigingizga yo'l ko'rsating (misol: "out of the front, turn left, directly opposite you — G").

tasks.title: Questions 6–10
tasks.type: Label the map. Write the correct letter, A–H
tasks.instr: Savollar tartibi = audio tartibi. Qalam bilan yo'lni chizib boring.
items: 6 recreation centre
7 health centre
8 swimming pool and sauna
9 health-food store
10 Jenny's Restaurant
why: "Go out of the main entrance and just along the main road to the east ... It's this T-shaped building". Sharqqa — C.
"Directly behind the main hospital building. So, if you go out of the back exit, it's just in front of you" — B.

"Walk out of the front ... go down that and turn left into Tye Road — you'll see the pool entrance at the end of that road, just beyond the line of trees". Tye Road oxiri, daraxtlardan keyin — H. Tuzoq: F — Tye Road boshida.
"Go beyond the turning for Tye Road and you'll see it on the right-hand corner, directly opposite another building" — E. Tuzoq: burilishga kirmaslik kerak.

"There's always the canteen inside the main building. But I would recommend ... Jenny's Restaurant ... head for the roundabout ... take the second turning on the left ... before the trees" — A. Tuzoq: kantina.
tasks.note: Ishlatilmagan harflar: D, F, G. G — kitobdagi 4-mashq misoli ("It's G"), uni savollarga javob deb yozmang.

listenings.title: Student's Book: recording script (Track 5–6) — ustoz uchun
intro: Tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqaring. Har javob gapini va tuzoq gapni alohida rang bilan ko'rsating; xaritada yo'lni skript bo'yicha chizing.

listenings.title: Workbook, Track 3: Health & Fitness in the Workplace conference (Q1–10)
listenings.qtype: Multiple choice + Plan labelling — imtihon rejimi
intro: Tashkilotchi konferensiya ishtirokchilariga dastur va bino rejasi haqida gapiradi. Avval 1-mashq: so'zlovchi qachon gapiryapti?
Keyin imtihondagidek: tayyorlanish vaqti, audio BIR MARTA. Rejada start nuqtasi — Main hall; Reception va Entrance hall ni oldindan toping.

tasks.title: 1-mashq: So'zlovchi qachon gapiryapti?
tasks.type: Choose A, B or C
tasks.instr: Ikkala topshiriqni ko'zdan kechiring va taxmin qiling, keyin audio bilan tekshiring.
items: 1 When is the speaker talking? A) at the beginning of a conference B) during the planning of a conference C) at the end of a conference
why: "Hello, and welcome to the conference" ... oxirida "OK, let's get started". Q6–10 da sessiyalar joyi so'raladi — ular hali boshlanmagan.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Savoldagi shartni belgilang: "in the past", "connection", "people attending", "in the sessions".
items: 1 The speaker says that the conference includes issues which A) were requested by participants. B) are seldom discussed. C) cause disagreement.
2 The speaker says that in the past, this subject A) caused problems in the workplace. B) was not something companies focused on. C) did not need to be addressed.
3 The speaker mentions a connection between health and fitness and A) keeping employees. B) employees' performance. C) a company's reputation.

4 What does the speaker say about the people attending the conference? A) Some of them may feel that there is not much they can learn. B) All of them have attended the conference before. C) Most of them are familiar with the speakers.
5 The speaker says that in the sessions, participants will A) work together in pairs. B) pretend to have various roles. C) describe real events.
why: "We've taken into account the answers that you gave us in our questionnaires ... the main ones that you indicated are important to you".
"Something that didn't get much attention not that many years ago" — "none of their business". Tuzoq: C — hozir kerak, oldin e'tibor berilmagan edi.
"A fit and healthy person does their job better" — ish samaradorligi. Tuzoq: "days off sick" — xodimni saqlash emas.
"Some of you may think you're already doing as much as you can ... but I promise you that you're all going to learn something new".
"In every session there will be a slot for people to talk about their own practices and experiences" — haqiqiy tajriba.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10
tasks.type: Label the plan. Write the correct letter, A–H
tasks.instr: Start — Main hall. Har yo'nalishdan keyin rejada barmog'ingizni suring.
items: 6 Setting Up a Fitness Centre
7 Healthy Eating Schemes
8 Transport Initiatives
9 Running Sports Teams
10 Conference Coordinator's Office
why: "Go out of the Main Hall here through those doors, turn right at reception and go along the corridor to the Taylor Room, which is on your left" — D.
"Go out of this hall the other way, through the doors at that end, and that takes you straight through to the Martin Suite" — H.
"Go out of those doors that bring you out opposite reception, turn left and left again into a corridor. The Fender Room is the third door on your right" — F.
"Go out of here, turn right at reception and then right again. The first door you come to on the left is the Gibson Suite" — A.
"To the left of Reception and along the corridor past the Entrance Hall ... you'll find my door at the end on your right" — C.
tasks.note: To'liq kalit: 1A 2B 3B 4A 5C 6D 7H 8F 9A 10C. Ishlatilmagan xonalar: B, E, G.

listenings.title: Workbook: recording script (Track 3) — ustoz uchun
intro: Skript bilan qayta tinglashda xato qilingan savollarning gapini topishga ishlatiladi. 6–10 uchun yo'nalishlarni rejada chizib ko'rsating.

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Hillside Organic Farm — open day
intro: Ferma egasi ochiq eshiklar kunida mehmonlarga ferma haqida gapiradi va xaritani tushuntiradi. Boshlashdan oldin o'quvchilarga 1–5-savollarni o'qish uchun 30 soniya bering. Ustoz skriptni bir marta, normal tezlikda (taxminan 150 so'z/daqiqa — jami 3–4 daqiqa) o'qiydi. MCQ qismidan keyin ("Right, let's look at the map" dan oldin) xaritaga qarash uchun 20–30 soniya pauza qiling.
Tinglashdan oldin xaritani doskaga chizing (pastdagi jadval: shimol — tepada). Start nuqtasi — Main barn.
transcript: SPEAKER: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Hillside Organic Farm. My name's Ruth, and my family has farmed this land for over a hundred years.

SPEAKER: People often ask how long we've been organic. We started changing about twelve years ago, but the process of conversion takes three years, so we've been fully certified organic for nine years now.

SPEAKER: And why did we change? Many visitors assume we did it for the money. It's true that organic vegetables sell at a higher price, and some of our regular customers were asking about it. But the real reason was the soil. Years of chemical fertiliser had left it hard and poor, and we wanted to bring it back to life.

SPEAKER: Now, a few things about today. Everything is free, so you don't need a ticket for anything. You're welcome to walk around the yard on your own, but if you'd like to see the fields, you'll need to join one of the guided walks, because the machinery is working out there. Boots are a good idea, but they're not essential.

SPEAKER: At twelve o'clock, our chef, Anna, will give a cooking demonstration. Last year she did bread-making, which was very popular, and a lot of you asked about cooking with children – we're planning that for next month. Today, though, she'll be showing you how to make the most of the vegetables that are in season right now: pumpkins, squash and beans.

SPEAKER: And one more thing. We opened our café two years ago, and we've always run composting days for local gardeners. But this year, for the first time, we're delivering weekly boxes of vegetables to homes in the town. There are leaflets about that at the shop.

SPEAKER: Right, let's look at the map. We're here, in the main barn, in the middle of the farm. Right next door to this barn, on its east side, is the farm shop. Please don't confuse it with the building further south on the same side, next to the yard – that's our packing shed, and it's closed to visitors.

SPEAKER: If you walk north from the barn, you'll come to the pond. The compost area is on the far side of the pond, to the west – in the north-west corner. The building on the eastern side of the pond is where we keep the beehives, so please keep away from that one.

SPEAKER: The hens used to live in the building on the west side of the main yard, but last spring we moved them to the south-west corner, right beside the main gate, where they have much more space. You can buy food for them at the shop.
SPEAKER: And that old hen house on the west side of the yard? It's now our café, so do go and try the soup.

SPEAKER: Finally, if anyone feels unwell, the first aid room is on the east side of the main gate, next to the car park. The toilets, by the way, are just beside this barn, on its west side. OK, enjoy your visit!

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Savoldagi shart so'zini belgilang: fully, main reason, must do, focus, new this year.
items: 1 How long has the farm been fully organic? A) three years B) nine years C) twelve years
2 What was the main reason the family changed to organic farming? A) Customers asked them to. B) They wanted to improve the soil. C) They wanted to earn more money.
3 What must visitors do if they want to see the fields? A) buy a ticket B) join a guided walk C) wear boots
4 Today's cooking demonstration will focus on A) using vegetables that are in season. B) baking bread. C) cooking with children.
5 What is new at the farm this year? A) a vegetable delivery service B) a café C) composting days
why: "We've been fully certified organic for nine years now". Tuzoq: 12 — o'zgarish boshlangan vaqt; 3 — o'tish davri.
"But the real reason was the soil". Tuzoq: A va C — "some customers were asking", "higher price" — lekin "but" dan keyin asl sabab.
"If you'd like to see the fields, you'll need to join one of the guided walks". Tuzoq: A — "you don't need a ticket"; C — "not essential".
"Today ... how to make the most of the vegetables that are in season right now". Tuzoq: B — o'tgan yil; C — keyingi oy.
"This year, for the first time, we're delivering weekly boxes of vegetables". Tuzoq: B — ikki yil oldin; C — "always".

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Hillside Organic Farm (xarita)
tasks.type: Label the map. Write the correct letter, A–H
tasks.instr: Jadval — xarita: shimol tepada, g'arb chapda. Start — Main barn. Har joy uchun harf yozing.
items: 6 Farm shop
7 Compost area
8 Hen house
9 Café
10 First aid room
why: "Right next door to this barn, on its east side, is the farm shop" — D. Tuzoq: F — "further south on the same side" — packing shed.
"On the far side of the pond, to the west – in the north-west corner" — A. Tuzoq: B — asalari uyalari.
"We moved them to the south-west corner, right beside the main gate" — G. Tuzoq: E — tovuqlar ILGARI shu yerda edi.
"That old hen house on the west side of the yard? It's now our café" — E.
"The first aid room is on the east side of the main gate, next to the car park" — H. Tuzoq: C — hojatxona ("beside this barn, on its west side").
tasks.note: 8- va 9-savol — eng yaxshi tuzoq namunasi: E harfi 8-savolda tuzoq, 9-savolda javob. O'quvchilarga "used to" iborasiga e'tibor berishni ayting.
head: West
Centre
East

homework_intro: Bugun Section 2 da ikki savol turini ketma-ket yechdik: avval MCQ, keyin xarita. Eng ko'p ball ikki joyda yo'qoladi — MCQ dagi "eshitilgan so'z" tuzog'i va xaritada yo'nalishni yo'qotish.

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: ustoz guruhga SB Track 6 audiosini va skript rasmini yuboradi. Track 6 ni (xarita qismi) skript bilan birga 3 marta tinglang va so'zlovchi bilan bir vaqtda takrorlang. Oxirgi marta o'zingizni yozib oling va ovozli xabarni guruhga yuboring.

Ikkinchi vazifa — diktant: ustoz guruhga WB Track 3 audiosini yuboradi. Uning ikkinchi qismini ("OK, now let's move on...") tinglang va 5 ta yo'nalish gapini to'liq yozib oling. Diktantni ustoz belgilagan muddatgacha guruhga yuboring; muddat tugagach ustoz skript rasmini yuboradi — solishtiring va xatolarni qizil rang bilan belgilang.

Uchinchi vazifa — o'z xaritangiz: akademiya atrofi, park yoki o'ylab topilgan mahalla xaritasini chizing (uy manzilingizni ko'rsatmang), 3 ta joyni harf bilan belgilang va 1 daqiqalik ovozli xabarda har biriga yo'l ko'rsating (opposite, beyond, turn left/right, the second turning). Xarita rasmi va ovozli xabarni guruhga yuboring; sherigingiz eshitib, topgan 3 ta harfni guruhga yozadi.

homework.title: Shadowing: SB Track 6
homework.instr: Ustoz guruhga SB Track 6 audiosi va skript rasmini yuboradi. Skript bilan 3 marta tinglash va takrorlash; oxirgisini yozib, guruhga yuborish.
homework.answers: Ustoz talaffuz va urg'uni tekshiradi (opposite, beyond, roundabout).

homework.title: Diktant: WB Track 3 (2-qism)
homework.instr: Ustoz guruhga WB Track 3 audiosini yuboradi. 5 ta yo'nalish gapini to'liq yozib, muddatgacha guruhga yuborish; keyin skript rasmi bilan solishtirish.
homework.answers: Diktant topshirish muddati tugagach ustoz WB skript rasmini guruhga yuboradi (oldinroq emas); o'quvchi o'zi solishtiradi, xatolar xatolar daftariga.

homework.title: O'z xaritangiz: ovozli yo'l ko'rsatish
homework.instr: Xarita (akademiya atrofi yoki o'ylab topilgan joy — uy manzili emas) + 3 joy + 1 daqiqalik ovozli xabar; sherik harflarni topadi.
homework.answers: Sherik topgan 3 ta harfni guruh chatiga yozadi; xarita muallifi to'g'ri yoki noto'g'ri ekanini javob xabarida tasdiqlaydi, ustoz normativni belgilaydi (3 dan 3 — 1 coin).

kahoot.q: You get 30 seconds before an MCQ + map section. What is the best use of this time?
options: Underline key words and find the start point on the map
Try to memorise every option in all five questions
Write a guessed answer next to every single question
Look only at the map and leave all the questions until later
kahoot.explain: Vaqtni ikkiga bo'ling: MCQ da shart so'zining tagiga chizing, xaritada start nuqtasi va mo'ljallarni toping.

kahoot.q: Question: 'What does the manager see as the MAIN problem?' Which phrase in the recording signals the answer?
options: "For example, a few of the staff…"
kahoot.explain: Savolda MAIN — javob "most", "the biggest", "above all" kabi ta'kid so'zlaridan keyin keladi.

kahoot.q: In a multiple-choice question, you hear the exact word from option A. What should you do?
options: Check the meaning — it may be a trap
Choose A immediately because the word matches
Cross out options B and C at once
kahoot.explain: Aynan eshitilgan so'z ko'pincha tuzoq; variant savoldagi shartga g'oya jihatidan mos kelishi kerak.

kahoot.q: 'Lots of people drive here, but honestly the easiest way is the number 12 bus.' What does the speaker recommend?
options: coming by car from the city
kahoot.explain: "But honestly" dan keyingi qism — so'zlovchining tavsiyasi; mashina — ko'pchilik nima qilishi, tavsiya emas.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'Hardly any of our visitors bother to book in advance.' Which option has the same meaning?
options: Very few visitors make a booking
Most visitors book a long time ahead
Visitors are required to book early
kahoot.explain: "Hardly any" = "very few"; javob variantda boshqa so'zlar bilan (paraphrase) beriladi.

kahoot.q: 'Walk past the bank, and the café is just beyond it.' Where is the café?
options: on the far side of the bank
just in front of the bank
just before you reach the bank
kahoot.explain: "Beyond" — narigi tomonida: bankdan o'tib, undan keyin.

kahoot.q: On the map you are walking SOUTH (down the page). The speaker says 'It's on your left.' Which side of the map is it on?
kahoot.explain: Janubga qarab yurganda chapingiz sharqda bo'ladi — xaritada o'ng tomonda.

kahoot.q: 'There's a car park next to the museum, but it's always full, so use the one behind the station.' Where should visitors park?
kahoot.explain: Birinchi aytilgan joy rad etildi; oxirgi tavsiya qilingan joy — javob.

kahoot.q: 'The gift shop used to be by the entrance, but last year it moved upstairs.' Where is the gift shop now?
kahoot.explain: "Used to" — eski joy; hozirgi joy "but" dan keyin aytiladi.

kahoot.q: A map has letters A–H, but there are only five questions. What does this tell you?
options: Three of the letters are not used
Every letter is used at least once
Two of the questions have no answer
kahoot.explain: 8 ta harf, 5 ta savol — 3 ta harf ortiqcha va tuzoq bo'lishi mumkin.

kahoot.q: In map labelling, in what order do you usually hear the answers?
options: in the same order as the questions
in alphabetical order of the letters
from the north of the map to the south
kahoot.explain: Javoblar odatda savollar tartibida keladi; harflar esa xaritada istalgan joyda bo'lishi mumkin.

kahoot.q: The recording is played only once, and you missed one place on the map. What should you do?
options: Guess a letter and follow the next directions
Stop and wait for the speaker to repeat that part
Leave all the other map questions blank
Go back and listen to the start of the map
kahoot.explain: Audio bir marta qo'yiladi: taxminiy harf yozing va keyingi mo'ljaldan davom eting.

kahoot.q: 'You need a ___ diet with fruit, vegetables, protein and a little fat.' Which word fits?
kahoot.explain: Balanced diet — muvozanatli ovqatlanish: har xil ovqat to'g'ri miqdorda.

kahoot.q: 'My doctor says I need an iron ___ because I don't get enough from food.' Which word fits?
kahoot.explain: Supplement — ovqatga qo'shimcha (vitamin, temir); complement va compliment boshqa ma'noda.

kahoot.q: Which sentence uses the word 'germ' correctly?
options: Germs spread fast on shared phones.
He has a real germ for football.
She boiled the germ with the rice.
Our germ starts at nine o'clock.
kahoot.explain: Germ — mikrob: kasallik tarqatadigan juda kichik organizm.

kahoot.q: Working nights one week and days the next, as many nurses do, is called ___.
kahoot.explain: Shift work — smenali ish: ish vaqti navbat bilan kunduz va tunga o'zgaradi.

kahoot.q: In British English, a circular junction where cars drive round in one direction is a ___.
kahoot.explain: Roundabout — aylanma yo'l (halqa); crossroads — oddiy chorraha.

kahoot.q: 'The company started a cycling ___ to encourage staff to ride to work.' Which word fits?
kahoot.explain: Initiative — tashabbus, yangi loyiha: biror muammoni hal qilish uchun boshlangan reja.

kahoot.q: 'When people are very tired, they often make ___ mistakes.' Which word fits?
kahoot.explain: Careless mistakes — e'tiborsizlik tufayli qilingan xatolar.

kahoot.q: Choosing an option only because you heard its exact word means that you ___.
kahoot.explain: Fall into a trap — tuzoqqa tushmoq; imtihonda eshitilgan so'z ko'pincha tuzoq bo'ladi.

lessons.title: Unit 3 Reading — Passage 3: Yes / No / Not Given + Summary (word list) + Multiple choice
lessons.grammar_topic: Passage 3 kombinatsiyasi: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN + Summary completion (so'zlar ro'yxati) + Multiple choice (A–D)
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 3 (Getting the message across) — til o'rganish, muloqot, yozuv uslubi
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 5–6.5: Student's Book, Unit 3, 30–32-betlar (Reading Section 3); Workbook, Unit 3, 20–22-betlar. Practice 1–3 — Jony Academy matnlari.
objectives: Passage 3 da uch savol turi kelganda har guruhni matnning qaysi qismiga tegishli ekanini 1–2 daqiqada aniqlash (xarita usuli).
YES / NO / NOT GIVEN da faktni emas, YOZUVCHINING FIKRI va da'vosini tekshirish; T/F/NG bilan farqini tushunish.
Summary sarlavhasidan matndagi kerakli xatboshini topish va ro'yxatdagi variantlarni so'z turi va ma'nosi bo'yicha qisqartirish.
MCQ (A–D) da savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oya bo'yicha joyni topish va "xatboshining maqsadi" savollariga javob berish.
Uch tur uchun 20 daqiqani to'g'ri taqsimlash: YNNG → summary → MCQ (yoki kitobdagi tartib bo'yicha).
materials: Student's Book, Unit 3, 30–32-betlar ("Why don't babies talk like adults?") — sinfda birga ishlanadi.
Workbook, Unit 3, 20–22-betlar ("Strictly English") — mustaqil mashq.
Practice 1–3 matnlari chop etilgan varaqlar (har o'quvchiga) — pastdagi Reading bo'limidan.
Taymer: Passage 3 uchun 20 daqiqa normasi doskaga yoziladi.
Doskada uch ustun: "YNNG → qaysi xatboshilar?", "Summary → sarlavha qaysi qismga?", "MCQ → kalit g'oya".
timeline: Kirish
SB 1-mashq: "Daddy go out", "Me go walkie" — bolalar nega shunday gapiradi? Sarlavha va kichik sarlavhadan matn nima haqida ekanini taxmin qilish.
Uch savol turi birga
Ustoz doskada: xarita usuli; YNNG — yozuvchi fikri; summary + so'zlar ro'yxati; MCQ A–D; vaqt taqsimoti; tuzoqlar.
Sinf mashqi
Mini-matn bo'yicha YES/NO/NOT GIVEN va SB summary bo'shliqlari uchun so'z turini aniqlab, variantlarni qisqartirish.
Student's Book: Why don't babies talk like adults?
Q1–14 birga ishlanadi: har javob uchun isbot gap va paraphrase juftligi.
Workbook: Strictly English
20 daqiqa mustaqil (imtihon rejimi), keyin javoblar izoh bilan tekshiriladi.
Practice 1
"Talking with our hands" — 18 daqiqa vaqt bilan, keyin qisqa tahlil.
Practice 2
"Is texting ruining young people's writing?" — 18 daqiqa, xatolar daftariga yoziladi.
Xulosa va vazifa
Practice 3 va 30-Day Reading Challenge (Day 30, Day 18) uyga; xatolar daftari.

intro: Passage 3 — imtihondagi eng uzun va eng qiyin matn. Unda faqat ma'lumot emas, yozuvchining FIKRI va dalillari ham bo'ladi. Shuning uchun Passage 3 da ko'pincha YES / NO / NOT GIVEN keladi, 14 ta savol esa odatda uch guruhga bo'linadi: bu darsda YNNG (1–4), summary + so'zlar ro'yxati (5–9) va multiple choice A–D (10–14).

Birinchi qadam — XARITA (1–2 daqiqa). Uchala guruhga ko'z yugurting: YNNG kalit so'zlari (babytalk, Behaviourists, one-word sentences), summary sarlavhasi ("Two theories about babytalk") va MCQ dagi ismlar/raqamlar (Snedeker, Harvard, "critical period", "seventh paragraph"). Har guruh matnning qaysi qismiga tegishli ekanini chetga yozib qo'ying.

YES / NO / NOT GIVEN — T/F/NG ning "fikr" versiyasi. Savol: "Yozuvchi shunday deydimi yoki shunday o'ylaydimi?" YES — yozuvchi rozi; NO — yozuvchi aksini aytadi; NOT GIVEN — yozuvchining bu masaladagi fikri matnda yo'q. Savollar matn tartibida keladi.

Summary + so'zlar ro'yxati (A–H): javob matndan ko'chirilmaydi — ro'yxatdagi HARF yoziladi. Ro'yxatda variantlar bo'shliqlardan ko'p (5 bo'shliq, 8 variant), ya'ni 3 ta ortiqcha. Ro'yxatdagi so'zlar ko'pincha matndagi so'zning paraphrase'i bo'ladi: "walk" → physical movement, "multiply/add" → mathematical knowledge.

Variantlarni qisqartirish: avval har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini aniqlang (ot, sifat, ot birikmasi), keyin grammatik jihatdan mos kelmaydiganlarini chiqarib tashlang. Qolgan 2–3 variant orasidan matndagi ma'no bo'yicha tanlang. Summary tartibi odatda matn tartibiga mos, lekin summary faqat bir-ikki xatboshini qamrashi mumkin.

MCQ (A–D): savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyani tagiga chizing va joyni toping. "What is the writer's main purpose in the seventh paragraph?" — butun xatboshining VAZIFASI so'raladi, bitta detal emas. Noto'g'ri variantlarda ko'pincha matndagi so'zlar bor, lekin ma'no boshqa ("China" → "English lessons in China").

Vaqt: Passage 3 ga 20 daqiqa. Taxminan: xarita 2 daqiqa, YNNG 5–6, summary 5–6, MCQ 6–7 daqiqa. Kitobdagi tartib har doim bir xil emas (30-Day Challenge Day 30 da MCQ → summary → YNNG) — xarita har doim birinchi.
formulas: extremely amused = few things are as funny
So'z bir xil ≠ ma'no bir xil
presentation: YES/NO/NG va TRUE/FALSE/NG farqi nima?
T/F/NG — matndagi FAKT haqida; YNNG — yozuvchining FIKRI yoki da'vosi haqida. Usul bir xil: isbot gapni topasiz.
Yozuvchi "I think" demasa-chi?
Yozuvchi o'z fikrini baholovchi so'zlar bilan ham bildiradi: "can't explain", "what is hard", "of course not", "shouldn't".
Summary da matndagi so'zni yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. So'zlar ro'yxati berilgan bo'lsa, faqat HARF yoziladi (C, F ...).
Ro'yxatdagi bir variant ikki bo'shliqqa mos keladi.
Odatda har variant bir marta ishlatiladi. Ikkala bo'shliqni matn bilan solishtiring — bittasiga aniqroq mos keladi.
MCQ savollari ham matn tartibidami?
Ha, odatda. 10-savol 7-xatbosh bo'lsa, 11–14 undan keyingi qismlarda.
"Main purpose" savolida qaysi variantni tanlayman?
Butun xatboshini qamraydigan variantni. Faqat bitta gapga mos variant — tuzoq.
notes: 5.0 da YNNG, summary va MCQ ni alohida o'rgangan edik. 6.0 da ularni bitta Passage 3 da birga yechamiz — asosiy ko'nikma xarita va vaqt taqsimoti.
Har javobdan keyin ikki savol bering: "isbot qaysi gapda?" va "ro'yxatdagi so'z matnda qanday aytilgan?" (masalan, physical movement = learn to walk).
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: SB summary ning 5-bo'shlig'i namuna (C). Nega A (vocabulary level) emasligini ular o'zi tushuntirsin — bu 7-bo'shliq uchun kerak.
mistakes: YNNG da o'z fikrini yozish ("men ham rozi emasman")
"What is hard for them to do is to explain these first words" → NO
MCQ da matndagi so'z bor variantni tanlash ("China")

how: CORE — til o'rganish va muloqot haqidagi asosiy so'zlar; STRONG — akademik matnlardagi terminlar; SUPER — Passage 3 dagi iboralar.
Har so'z bilan o'quvchi o'z til o'rganish tajribasidan bitta gap tuzsin: "My English vocabulary grew gradually after I started reading."
core: Children acquire their first language without lessons.
Language acquisition starts in the first year of life.
Tilni o'zlashtirish hayotning birinchi yilida boshlanadi.
Babies imitate the sounds they hear.
She speaks English almost like a native speaker.
U inglizchani deyarli ona tili sohibidek gapiradi.

Kurs ingliz tilidagi bilim darajangizni tekshiradi.

Har bir bola bir so'zli bosqichdan o'tadi.

Learning to write well is a gradual process.
Try to express your idea in one sentence.
Fikringizni bitta gapda ifodalashga harakat qiling.
strong: The study tested two competing hypotheses.
After a certain threshold, children start combining words.
Ma'lum chegaradan keyin bolalar so'zlarni birlashtira boshlaydi.
A baby's brain is still immature.
Good writers try to avoid ambiguity.
Yaxshi yozuvchilar noaniqlikdan qochishga harakat qiladi.

Inshongiz har qanday o'quvchiga tushunarli bo'lishi kerak.

Shifokorlar ko'pincha bemor tushunmaydigan atamalarni ishlatadi.

Bir so'zli bosqich tezda ikki so'zli bosqichga o'rin beradi.
Ular sekin bo'lsa ham, oldinga siljishdi.

class_ex.title: Yozuvchi nima deydi? — mini-matn
class_ex.instr: Ustoz doskaga yozadi: "Many parents believe that watching cartoons in English will make their children fluent. I doubt it. Children certainly pick up some words and phrases this way, but real fluency requires conversation, not just listening." Har gap uchun javob va isbotni ayting.
items: Children can learn some English words from cartoons.
Cartoons are the best way to become fluent in a language.
Most parents in Uzbekistan let their children watch cartoons in English.
Listening on its own is enough to become fluent.
why: "Children certainly pick up some words and phrases this way". "Certainly" — yozuvchi rozi.
"I doubt it" — yozuvchi ota-onalar fikriga qo'shilmaydi.
Ota-onalar fikri bor, lekin qaysi davlatda va nechta ota-ona ekani haqida yozuvchi hech narsa demaydi.
"Real fluency requires conversation, not just listening" — teskari.
class_ex.note: 1- va 2-gapni solishtiring: ikkalasi ham multfilm haqida, lekin yozuvchi birinchisiga rozi, ikkinchisiga qarshi. YNNG da aynan shu nozik farq tekshiriladi.

class_ex.title: So'z turi → variantlarni qisqartirish (SB, 6–7-mashq)
class_ex.instr: SB dagi "Two theories about babytalk" summary'sida 6–9 bo'shliqlar uchun javob bermasdan: qanday so'z kerak va ro'yxatdagi qaysi 2–3 variant grammatik jihatdan mos keladi?
items: 6 — "other abilities such as ___"
7 — "a child's ___ is the key factor"
8 — "some key steps have to occur ... before ___ occurs"
9 — "Children's ___ develops in the same way"
why: "Abilities such as" — misol qobiliyat bo'lishi kerak: physical movement yoki mathematical knowledge. "Time", "teaching" qobiliyat emas.
"A child's ___" — bolaga tegishli narsa: vocabulary level yoki attention.
"___ occurs" — sodir bo'ladigan jarayon: sentence formation yoki learning.
"develops in the same way" — rivojlanadigan bilim: mathematical knowledge (vocabulary level 7 ga ketgan).
class_ex.note: Mashqdan keyin o'quvchilar matnni o'qib yakuniy tanlovni qiladi (javoblar SB blokida). Maqsad — 8 variantdan boshlamaslik, 2–3 variantdan boshlash.

found it easy to work out

tasks.title: Questions 1–4
tasks.type: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: YES — gap yozuvchining fikriga mos; NO — gap yozuvchining fikriga zid; NOT GIVEN — yozuvchi bu haqida nima deb o'ylashini matndan bilib bo'lmaydi. SB 4–5-mashq: tagiga chizilgan so'zlar (amused, Behaviourists, conversations, one-word sentences) joyni topishga yordam beradi.
items: People are extremely amused when they see a baby talk like an adult.
Behaviourists of the early 20th century argued that children learn to speak by copying adults.
Children have more conversations with adults than with other children.
Scientists have found it easy to work out why babies use one-word sentences.
why: "Few things are as funny as a baby who talks like an adult". "Extremely amused" = "few things are as funny".
Oldingi gapda "children learn to talk by copying what they hear", keyin: Behaviourism "made exactly this argument". "Early 20th century" = "the first half of the 20th century".
"Conversational" so'zi bor ("toddlers aren't as conversational as adults"), lekin bolalar kim bilan ko'proq gaplashishi taqqoslanmagan.
"What is hard for them to do is to explain these first words". Tuzoq: "it's easy for scientists" ham bor, lekin u copycat nazariyasi ishlamasligini ko'rsatish haqida.
tasks.note: 4-savol — darsning asosiy tuzog'i: "easy" so'zi matnda bor. O'quvchidan "easy nima haqida, hard nima haqida?" deb so'rang.

tasks.title: Questions 5–9 — Two theories about babytalk
tasks.type: Complete the summary using the list of words and phrases, A–H.
tasks.instr: Sarlavha "Two theories" — faqat ikki nazariya tasvirlangan xatboshilarni o'qing ("Over the past half-century..." dan "The difference between these theories..." gacha). Javob — harf. 5-savol kitobda namuna sifatida berilgan (C).
items: 5 One theory: a young child's brain needs (5) to master language ...
6 ... in the same way that it does to master other abilities such as (6).
7 The second theory states that a child's (7) is the key factor.
8 Some key steps have to occur in a logical sequence before (8) occurs.
9 Children's (9) develops in the same way.
why: "Their immature brains can't handle adult speech ... before their brains are ready" — miya yetilishi uchun vaqt kerak.
"Children don't learn to walk until their bodies are ready". Walk = physical movement. Tuzoq: E — bu ikkinchi nazariyaning misoli.

"Don't usually begin speaking in two-word sentences until they've learned a certain number of single words" — so'zlar soni, ya'ni lug'at darajasi. Keyingi xatboshi ham buni tasdiqlaydi: "what matters is ... the number of words you know".
"Begin speaking in two-word sentences" — gap tuzish (sentence formation).
"Children learn to multiply after they have learned to add" — matematika ham bosqichma-bosqich.
tasks.note: Ro'yxatda uchta ortiqcha variant bor (D, G, H). O'quvchi har bir tanlovi uchun matndagi misolni aytishi kerak: walk, single words, two-word sentences, add/multiply.

tasks.title: Questions 10–14
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D
tasks.instr: SB 8-mashq: kalit g'oyani tagiga chizing (seventh paragraph, Snedeker, differed, Harvard finding, critical period) va joyni toping.
items: 10 What is the writer's main purpose in the seventh paragraph? A) to give reasons why adopted children were used in the study B) to reject the view that adopted children need two languages C) to argue that culture affects the way children learn a language D) to justify a particular approach to language learning

11 Snedeker, Geren and Shafto based their study on children who A) were finding it difficult to learn English. B) had come from a number of language backgrounds. C) were learning English at a later age than US children. D) had taken English lessons in China.

12 What aspect of the adopted children's language development differed from that of US-born children? A) their first words B) the way they learnt English C) the rate at which they acquired language D) the point at which they started producing sentences

13 What did the Harvard finding show? A) Not all toddlers use babytalk. B) Language learning takes place in ordered steps. C) Some children need more conversation than others. D) Not all brains work in the same way.

14 When the writer says 'critical period', he means a period when A) studies produce useful results. B) adults need to be taught like children. C) immigrants want to learn another language. D) language learning takes place effectively.
why: 7-xatbosh "In 2007, researchers at Harvard..." bilan boshlanadi va nega xalqaro asrab olingan bolalar tanlanganini tushuntiradi: "All of these factors make them an ideal population".
"These children began learning English at an older age than US natives". D — tuzoq: bolalar Xitoydan asrab olingan, u yerda ingliz tili darsi haqida gap yo'q.
"The adoptees then went through the same stages ... albeit at a faster clip". Faster clip = tezroq sur'at (rate). A va D bir xil bo'lgan.
"The one-word stage will give way to the two-word stage and so on" — til bosqichma-bosqich o'rganiladi.
"A 'critical period' ... after which it cannot proceed with full success to fluency" — ya'ni undan oldin o'rganish samarali.
tasks.note: 10-savolda xatboshilarni doskada birga sanang: 1 — e-trade reklamasi, 2 — copying, 3 — However, 4 — mental-development, 5 — stages-of-language (basketbol misoli shu xatboshi ichida), 6 — The difference, 7 — In 2007.

tasks.title: 1-mashq: summary qaysi xatboshilarda?
tasks.type: Og'zaki

answers: 4- va 5-xatboshilar ("Can English, though, ever be fixed?" va "It is to these standards...")
why: Summary da "reference books", "a century", "his own book" bor — bular OED, "a century ago" va "Strictly English" haqidagi ikki xatboshida.

tasks.title: Questions 1–4
tasks.type: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: YES — gap yozuvchining fikriga mos; NO — gap yozuvchining fikriga zid; NOT GIVEN — yozuvchi bu haqida nima deb o'ylashini matndan bilib bo'lmaydi.
items: The mistakes made by his colleagues are minor ones.
It is difficult to explain why using correct English is important.
English grammar has a different function from the grammar of other languages.
Word order may be as important as the choice of words used.
why: "Happily, these are reasonably rare" — xatolar KAM uchraydi (soni), lekin ular kichik yoki jiddiy ekani (darajasi) haqida hech narsa yo'q.
"The latter, being a matter for debate, is less straightforward". "The latter" = why it matters.
"The logic that drove it and that was common to all the other languages I knew" — boshqa tillar bilan umumiy.

Javob: YES. Yozuvchi so'z tanlashni ("why would a writer choose that noun rather than another") va so'z tartibini ("Was the ambiguity in a certain order of words deliberate or accidental?") bir qatorga qo'yib, ikkalasi haqida: "The whole question of communication is rooted in such things" deydi — ya'ni so'z tartibi ham so'z tanlash kabi muhim. NOT GIVEN qabul qilinmaydi: yozuvchi bu masalada fikrini aniq bildirgan.
tasks.note: 1-savol — kuchli NOT GIVEN: "rare" (kam) va "minor" (kichik) har xil tushuncha. O'quvchidan ikkalasining farqini o'zbekcha so'rang.

tasks.title: Questions 5–9 — The rules of English
tasks.type: Complete the summary using the list of words, A–H.
tasks.instr: Javob — harf. Summary 4–5-xatboshilarga tegishli.
items: 5 English should not be considered something (5), and this will always be the case.
6 Reference books for over a century were produced by (6) people.
7 The established rules that are in (7) use and that people are accustomed to.
8 He wants his book to be (8) as a way of improving people's ability.
9 Grammar should not be a (9) subject.
why: "Can English, though, ever be fixed? Of course not" — til o'zgarib turadi, doimiy emas.
"Learned men, many of whom contributed to the OED, wrote grammars a century ago". Learned = knowledgeable. G (historic) — tuzoq: "a century ago" vaqtni bildiradi, odamlarni emas.
"A standard that people recognise and are comfortable with" — umumiy qo'llanishdagi qoidalar.
"Help people towards a capable grasp of the English tongue" — foydali bo'lish.
"English grammar shouldn't be a matter for debate". Matter for debate = controversial.

tasks.title: Questions 10–14
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D
tasks.instr: Kalit g'oya: private language, bilingual academics, writing of academics, language in journals, the Internet.
items: 10 The writer says that some groups of people use a 'private language' because A) they do not want outsiders to be able to understand them. B) they want to show their superiority over other groups. C) they want to impress other members of their group. D) they do not want to use the same language as other groups.

11 According to the writer, some academics are capable of A) making sense to people outside their group. B) writing very clearly for learned journals. C) changing the way they communicate within their own group. D) explaining other people's work to the general public.

12 When discussing the writing of academics about their research, the writer emphasises A) his own lack of knowledge of the academic world. B) his desire to understand what they describe. C) his sympathy for some of the academics. D) his dislike for the style used in their writing.

13 The writer says that the kind of language used by academics in journals A) is becoming more widely understood by non-academics. B) is attracting a lot of criticism from other academics. C) will only change if they are forced to change it. D) appeals only to highly intelligent people.

14 The writer's opinion of the Internet is that A) it is making people more aware of the poor use of language. B) it is encouraging standards of language use to fall. C) it is enabling people to compare good and poor use of language. D) it is making it harder for good writing to get published.
why: "In order to be taken seriously by their peers". Peers = members of their group. A — tuzoq: "not because the outsiders are stupid".
"Some academics, however, are bilingual ... they can rediscover the knack of writing reasonably plain English" — gazeta uchun, ya'ni tashqi o'quvchiga. B — teskari: journallarda aniq yozishmaydi.
"Ugly and barbaric ... repetitious, long-winded, abstract and abstruse" — uslubni yoqtirmaydi.
"Will not easily be discouraged, unless what is considered acceptable within their disciplines changes" — faqat qoidalar o'zgarsa o'zgaradi.
"Having a harmful effect on the language and causing it to be corrupted". D — tuzoq: nashr qilish haqida gap bor, lekin u internetdan OLDINgi holat.

readings.title: Practice 1: Talking with our hands
readings.qtype: Yes/No/Not Given (1–4) + Summary, word list (5–9) + Multiple choice A–D (10–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi)
text: Watch anyone speaking on the telephone and you will probably see their hands moving, even though the listener cannot see them. For a long time, this was treated as a curious habit, a kind of nervous decoration added to the real business of speech. In my view, that explanation has always been unconvincing. If gestures existed only to help listeners, we would expect people to stop gesturing as soon as nobody could see them. They do not. Nor is the habit limited to a few especially expressive individuals; almost everyone does it, whatever their personality or background.

The strongest evidence comes from people who have never seen a gesture at all. In one well-known study, researchers asked children who had been blind from birth to describe routes and to explain simple puzzles. The children moved their hands as they spoke, using much the same kinds of movements as sighted children, and they did so even when they knew that their listener was also blind. Gesture, it seems, is not simply copied from others. The researchers also noted that the children gestured more when the task was harder, which is exactly what one would expect if gesture were helping them to think. It appears to be part of the way that speakers organise what they want to say.

This idea is supported by experiments in which people are prevented from moving their hands. When speakers are asked to sit on their hands or hold an object while describing a picture, they tend to pause more often and to have greater difficulty finding words, especially words for shapes, directions and movements. Not every study has found this effect, and its size varies considerably from one experiment to another. Nevertheless, the general pattern suggests that gesture helps speakers to find language, not just to deliver it.

Children offer a further window on the relationship. Long before they can produce two-word sentences, many toddlers combine a single word with a pointing gesture: they say 'cup' while pointing at their mother, meaning something like 'Mummy's cup'. Researchers who have followed children over several months report that those who produce these word-plus-gesture combinations early also tend to begin speaking in two-word sentences earlier. Gesture, in other words, may allow children to express an idea before they have the grammar to put it into words. Parents, of course, respond to these combinations, often by turning the idea into a full sentence — 'Yes, that's Mummy's cup' — so gesture may also invite exactly the kind of language that children need to hear.

None of this means that gestures are the same everywhere. Travellers quickly discover that a hand signal which is harmless at home can be rude elsewhere, and even the way people point differs between cultures: in some communities, people point with their lips or chin rather than with a finger. The amount of gesturing also varies. Speakers of some languages are famous for using their hands a great deal, although the popular belief that certain nationalities gesture more than others has been examined far less carefully than one might expect.

What are the practical lessons? Teachers have begun to take gesture seriously. In classroom studies, children who were taught a maths strategy with both words and gestures remembered it better several weeks later than children who were taught with words alone. I would not go so far as to say that every lesson should be accompanied by carefully planned hand movements; forced gestures can distract as much as they help. But teachers who fold their arms while explaining a difficult idea may be making it harder for their students than necessary.

Language learners, too, might benefit. A learner who cannot remember a word can often keep a conversation going by describing it with their hands, and the listener's response frequently supplies the missing word. Rather than being a sign of weakness, this is exactly the kind of strategy that successful communicators use. The hands, it turns out, are not an accessory to speech. They are one of the places where speech begins.
glossary: toddler — endi yura boshlagan bola (1–3 yosh)
accessory — qo'shimcha bezak, ikkinchi darajali narsa
paraphrases: mainly for the benefit of the listener
existed only to help listeners ... They do not (qarshi ma'no)
not always done with the hand
with their lips or chin rather than with a finger
the kind of strategy that successful communicators use

tasks.title: Questions 1–4
tasks.type: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: YES — gap yozuvchining fikriga mos; NO — gap yozuvchining fikriga zid; NOT GIVEN — yozuvchi bu haqida nima deb o'ylashini matndan bilib bo'lmaydi. Savollar 1–5-xatboshilarga tegishli.
items: Gestures exist mainly for the benefit of the listener.
Blind children continue to gesture even when speaking to someone who cannot see.
All studies have found that speakers have difficulty finding words when their hands are held still.
The belief that some nationalities gesture more than others is probably false.
why: "If gestures existed only to help listeners, we would expect people to stop gesturing as soon as nobody could see them. They do not." — yozuvchi bu fikrni rad etadi; uning fikricha, imo-ishora avvalo gapiruvchining o'ziga yordam beradi ("part of the way that speakers organise what they want to say"; "gesture helps speakers to find language, not just to deliver it"). Diqqat: matnda "only", gapda "mainly" — javobni yozuvchining umumiy fikri hal qiladi: imo-ishora asosan tinglovchi uchun emas, demak NO.
"They did so even when they knew that their listener was also blind".
"Not every study has found this effect". "All" javobni NO qiladi.
Yozuvchi bu fikr "far less carefully" tekshirilganini aytadi, lekin u noto'g'ri deb da'vo qilmaydi. Kam tekshirilgan ≠ noto'g'ri.
tasks.note: 4-savol — Passage 3 ga xos NOT GIVEN: yozuvchi masalaga munosabat bildiradi (kam o'rganilgan), lekin savoldagi xulosani (noto'g'ri) chiqarmaydi.

tasks.title: Questions 5–9 — Gesture and learning
tasks.type: Complete the summary using the list of words, A–H.
tasks.instr: Summary 4- va 6-xatboshilarga tegishli. Javob — harf.
items: 5 Young children often use a single word together with (5) before they can make two-word sentences.
6 Children who do this early usually start to use (6) sooner.
7 Gesture seems to let children express an idea before they have learnt the necessary (7).
8 Children taught a maths strategy with words and gestures showed better (8) of it weeks later.
9 The writer warns that gestures which are not natural may cause (9).
why: "Combine a single word with a pointing gesture". H — tuzoq: yuz ifodasi matnda yo'q.
"Begin speaking in two-word sentences earlier". Two-word sentences = word combinations.
"Before they have the grammar to put it into words". E — tuzoq: vocabulary mantiqan mos, lekin matnda grammar.
"Remembered it better several weeks later" — xotira.
"Forced gestures can distract as much as they help". Not natural = forced.

tasks.title: Questions 10–14
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D
tasks.instr: "Main purpose" savolida butun xatboshini qamraydigan variantni tanlang.
items: 10 What is the writer's main purpose in the first paragraph? A) to describe how people behave on the telephone B) to challenge a traditional explanation of gesture C) to argue that listeners ignore gestures D) to explain why people become nervous when speaking

readings.title: Practice 2: Is texting ruining young people's writing?
readings.qtype: Yes/No/Not Given (1–4) + Summary, word list (5–9) + Multiple choice A–D (10–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi)
text: Every few years, a newspaper announces that young people can no longer write. The cause changes — television, then computer games, now mobile phones — but the complaint remains the same. Text messages, with their missing vowels, abbreviations and absent punctuation, are currently blamed for everything from poor spelling in school essays to the decline of the handwritten letter. It is an easy argument to make, and in my view it is largely mistaken.

To begin with, the features that alarm critics are not new. Abbreviations such as 'etc.' and 'Mr' have been used for centuries, and Victorian telegrams, which were charged by the word, were at least as compressed as any modern text message. Word puzzles that replace words with letters and numbers were popular long before the first mobile phone. What is new is the quantity: young people today probably write more words each day than any previous generation of teenagers, even if many of those words are short.

Researchers have tested the claim directly. In several studies with primary-school children, those who used more textisms — the abbreviations typical of text messages — did not have worse spelling than their classmates. In some cases, the opposite was true: children who were good at producing textisms were also better at reading and spelling. This makes sense when one considers that writing 'gr8' for 'great' requires a child to understand how sounds relate to letters. You cannot break a rule creatively unless you know what the rule is.

That said, the picture is not entirely positive. Studies of older teenagers and university students have produced more mixed results, and some teachers report that informal features occasionally appear in formal work. Such slips are real, but they tend to be fairly rare, and they are usually corrected once they are pointed out. The more important skill, it seems to me, is not avoiding informal writing altogether but knowing when it is appropriate.

Linguists call this skill register awareness: the ability to adjust one's language to suit the situation. Every competent speaker does this constantly. We do not speak to a job interviewer in the same way that we speak to a younger brother, and nobody concludes from our relaxed conversations at home that we are unable to speak politely. Written language is no different. A student who writes 'c u l8r' to a friend and a carefully structured paragraph in an exam is not confused; they are switching between registers, just as adults do. The same person may use three or four different registers in a single afternoon — in a lecture, in a message to a friend, on the phone to a bank — without noticing that they have done anything unusual.

Where, then, should concern be directed? If there is a genuine problem, it may lie less in how young people write than in how much they read. Short messages, however frequent, do not expose readers to the long, complex sentences found in books and quality journalism. A teenager who writes hundreds of messages a day but never reads anything longer than a paragraph may well struggle when asked to produce an extended argument. The solution, however, is not to ban phones but to make sure that sustained reading remains part of every young person's week. Reading and writing develop together, and the vocabulary and sentence patterns that students meet in books are the ones they later reproduce in their own essays.

Language has always changed, and older generations have always worried about it. Texting has added a new variety of English to the many that already exist; it has not replaced the others. Rather than treating it as a threat, schools could use it as a starting point for discussing how and why we choose different words for different audiences. A pupil who can explain why 'u' is acceptable in a message but not in a job application has understood something important about language.

write more words each day than any previous generation

changing language to suit the situation
adjust one's language to suit the situation

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Learning a language as an adult — is it too late?
readings.qtype: Multiple choice A–D (1–4) + Summary, word list (5–9) + Yes/No/Not Given (10–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi), uy vazifasi
text: It is widely believed that children are better language learners than adults. The belief is so common that many adults never start learning a language at all, assuming that the chance has passed. There is some truth in the idea, but it has been exaggerated, and the way it is usually expressed hides several important distinctions.

The first distinction is between the speed of learning and the final level reached. When researchers compare children and adults over the first months of learning, adults usually make faster progress. They can apply rules consciously, use a dictionary, and draw on what they already know about how languages work. In classroom studies lasting a year or two, teenagers and adults often do better than young children on tests of grammar and reading. Older learners also tend to be better at learning vocabulary quickly. Children's advantage appears only in the long term: those who start young and spend many years surrounded by a language are much more likely to end up sounding like native speakers.

The second distinction concerns which part of language we are talking about. Pronunciation is where age seems to matter most. People who begin learning a language after their early teens very rarely lose their foreign accent completely, however long they live in the new country. Even so, many people with a noticeable accent speak fluently and are perfectly easy to understand, and for most purposes that is what matters. Grammar shows a weaker connection with age, and vocabulary shows little connection at all: adults continue to learn new words in their first language throughout their lives, and there is no obvious reason why a second language should be different.

A third distinction is between learning a language and living in it. Much of the research that supports the idea of a 'critical period' comes from immigrants, whose age on arrival is compared with their eventual level. But age on arrival is linked to many other factors. A child who arrives at eight goes to a local school, makes local friends and hears the language all day. An adult who arrives at thirty may work long hours with people who speak their first language, and may feel embarrassed about making mistakes. It is difficult to know how much of the adult's lower final level is caused by the brain and how much by circumstances.

One large online study, which collected grammar test results from hundreds of thousands of people, suggested that the ability to learn grammar remains strong until late adolescence and declines only after that. The researchers were careful to point out that this does not mean adults cannot learn grammar well; it means that reaching a native-like level becomes gradually less likely, not impossible. In my opinion, this is the most useful way to think about age: as something that changes the odds rather than something that closes a door.

What does this mean for an adult who wants to learn a language? First, the goal matters. If the aim is to sound exactly like a native speaker, starting late is a genuine disadvantage. If the aim is to communicate effectively, read, work or study in the language, adults are in a strong position, especially at the beginning. Second, adults should make use of their strengths: their ability to organise their study, to understand explanations and to notice patterns. Third, they should try to recreate some of the conditions children enjoy — plenty of exposure, meaningful conversation and, perhaps most importantly, a willingness to make mistakes without feeling foolish.

It is sometimes said that adults learn languages badly because they are afraid of looking silly. There may be something in this. Children rarely worry about whether their sentences are correct; they simply want to be understood. Adults, by contrast, often stay silent rather than risk an error, and silence is the one thing that guarantees no progress. Adults who can recover a little of that attitude may find that the door they thought had closed was never really locked.

kahoot.q: Reading Passage 3 has three question groups: YES/NO/NOT GIVEN, a summary and multiple choice. What should you do first?
options: Find which part of the text each group covers
Read the whole passage slowly twice
Underline every unknown word in the text
kahoot.explain: Avval xarita: 1–2 daqiqada har savol guruhi matnning qaysi xatboshilariga tegishli ekanini belgilaymiz.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Some claim that e-books will soon replace paper books. I find this hard to believe.' Statement: 'Paper books will soon disappear.'
options: NO – the writer doubts this claim
YES – the text mentions this claim
NOT GIVEN – no dates are given
NOT GIVEN – e-books are not described
kahoot.explain: "I find this hard to believe" — yozuvchi da'voga qo'shilmaydi, demak NO. Da'voning matnda tilga olinishi YES degani emas.

kahoot.q: Text: 'In my view, the examples in this new dictionary are exceptionally clear.' Statement: 'The new dictionary is better value than older ones.'
options: NOT GIVEN – value is not discussed
YES – the writer praises the dictionary
NO – the writer criticises older dictionaries
YES – clear examples mean better value
kahoot.explain: Yozuvchi misollarni maqtaydi, lekin narx yoki qiymat haqida fikr bildirmaydi — NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Online courses are probably the most flexible way to study.' Statement: 'Online courses are more flexible than other ways of studying.'
options: YES – a cautious view is still a view
NOT GIVEN – the writer is not certain
NOT GIVEN – other ways are not named
kahoot.explain: "Probably" — ehtiyotkor ohang, lekin baribir yozuvchining fikri; gap unga mos, demak YES.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Only a small number of schools still teach Latin.' Statement: 'Most schools still teach Latin.'
options: YES – both mention schools teaching Latin
NOT GIVEN – the number of schools is unknown
NOT GIVEN – the writer gives no opinion
kahoot.explain: "Only a small number" va "most" bir-biriga zid — javob NO.

kahoot.q: A YES/NO/NOT GIVEN statement uses the same word as the passage, e.g. 'popular'. What does this tell you?
options: Nothing yet – check the whole claim
The answer is almost certainly YES
The answer cannot be NOT GIVEN
The answer is almost certainly NO
kahoot.explain: Bir xil so'z bir xil da'vo degani emas: so'z matnda nimaga tegishli ekanini va yozuvchi nima deyotganini tekshiramiz.

kahoot.q: Passage: 'Learners seldom notice their own errors.' Which sentence has the same meaning?
options: Learners rarely spot their own mistakes.
Learners never notice their own mistakes.
kahoot.explain: seldom = rarely (kamdan-kam), errors = mistakes; "never" — mutlaq so'z, ma'noni o'zgartiradi.

kahoot.q: A summary gives a box of options A–H. What do you write on the answer sheet?
options: The letter of the correct option
The word or words from the passage
The full phrase copied from the box
Both the letter and the phrase
kahoot.explain: Variantlar ro'yxati berilgan bo'lsa, faqat HARF yoziladi (masalan, F); so'z yoki ibora yozilsa (matndan ham, ro'yxatdan ham) — 0 ball.

kahoot.q: Before you look at the options in the box, what should you decide for each gap?
options: What type of word the gap needs
How many words the passage uses
Which option is the longest one
Whether the gap is near the title
kahoot.explain: Avval bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini (ot, sifat, fe'l) aniqlaymiz — shunda 8 variantdan 2–3 tasi qoladi.

kahoot.q: Summary: 'Many teenagers feel too ___ to speak in front of the class.' Which option fits the gap grammatically?
kahoot.explain: "feel too ___ to ..." qolipida sifat kerak: nervous. Silence, courage, anxiety — otlar.

kahoot.q: A paragraph describes three studies and ends: 'All of this suggests that sleep improves memory.' What is its main purpose?
options: To support a claim about sleep and memory
To describe one study in great detail
To criticise the methods of sleep research
To compare the results of three researchers
kahoot.explain: Main purpose — butun xatboshining vazifasi: uchta tadqiqot bitta xulosani (uyqu xotirani yaxshilaydi) qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

kahoot.q: In a multiple-choice question, one option repeats several exact words from the passage. What should you think?
options: It may be a trap – compare the meaning
It is almost always the correct answer
It must be wrong because it copies the text
It is correct if it is the longest option
kahoot.explain: Tuzoq variantlar ko'pincha matndagi so'zlarni takrorlaydi, lekin ma'no boshqa — variantni isbot gap bilan solishtiramiz.

kahoot.q: 'Children acquire their first language without lessons.' Here 'acquire' means…
kahoot.explain: acquire — egallamoq, o'zlashtirmoq: bola ona tilini darssiz, tabiiy ravishda o'zlashtiradi.

kahoot.q: Babies ___ the sounds that they hear around them.
kahoot.explain: imitate — taqlid qilmoq: chaqaloqlar eshitgan tovushlarini takrorlaydi.

kahoot.q: 'Fluency' in a language is the ability to…
options: understand every word of a text
pronounce words like a native speaker
kahoot.explain: fluency — ravonlik: ko'p to'xtamasdan, erkin gapirish.

kahoot.q: 'The course tests your proficiency in English.' The course tests…
kahoot.explain: proficiency — bilim yoki malaka darajasi (a high level of proficiency).

kahoot.q: Special words used by one profession, often hard for outsiders to understand, are called…
kahoot.explain: jargon — kasbiy atamalar: faqat shu soha odamlari yaxshi tushunadigan so'zlar.

kahoot.q: A sentence that can be understood in two different ways contains…
kahoot.explain: ambiguity — noaniqlik, ikki ma'nolilik.

kahoot.q: 'They made progress, albeit slowly.' 'Albeit' is closest in meaning to…
kahoot.explain: albeit = although (garchi ... bo'lsa ham): ular sekin bo'lsa ham oldinga siljishdi.

kahoot.q: 'She used simple words to get her message across.' She wanted people to…
kahoot.explain: get the message across — fikrni tushunarli qilib yetkazmoq.

Tayyorlanish → Track 10 (Q1–4) → matching va short answer ni o'qish → Track 11 (Q5–10) → javoblar izoh bilan.
Workbook: Track 4
Imtihon rejimi: 1-mashq, tayyorlanish, audio BIR MARTA, 10 savol.
Jony Academy mashqi
"Planning a group presentation" — ustoz va ikki o'quvchi rollarda o'qiydi, qolganlar 10 savolga javob beradi; rol o'qigan ikkovi tahlilda isbot gaplarni skriptdan ko'rsatadi.
Skript bilan tahlil
Xato qilingan savollar skriptda topiladi; rad etilgan variant va paraphrase belgilanadi.
Xulosa va vazifa
Uyga: shadowing, diktant va paraphrase ro'yxati.

intro: Section 3 — o'quv mavzusidagi suhbat: odatda talaba(lar) va o'qituvchi (tutor), ba'zan uch kishi. Unda faqat ma'lumot emas, FIKR va BAHO ham bo'ladi: "a bit dull", "went down well", "I wasn't sure they could be justified". Imtihonda Section 3 (21–30-savollar) odatda ikki, ba'zan uch savol turidan iborat; bugungi kitob mashqlarida uchalasi ketma-ket keladi: TWO letters, matching va short answer.

Tayyorlanish vaqtini uchga bo'ling. TWO letters: savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyani tagiga chizing ("WILL students do", "MUST check", "IMPRESSIVE according to the tutor"). Matching: sarlavha va variantlardagi kalit so'zlarni belgilang (repetitive, long time to write, shorter, well structured, relevant, popular). Short answer: so'z chegarasini doiraga oling.

Choose TWO letters (A–E): beshta variantning deyarli hammasi suhbatda tilga olinadi. Uch variant tuzoq bo'ladi: taklif qilinib RAD ETILADI ("something from one of the textbooks" → "a much better idea"), kelajakdagi yoki boshqa ishga tegishli bo'ladi ("the starting point for a whole other piece of work"), yoki salbiy baholanadi. Javoblar variantlar tartibida emas, suhbat tartibida keladi. Har harf — alohida ball; ikkala harfni istalgan tartibda yozish mumkin.

Matching (A–F): savollar (5, 6, 7, 8) suhbat tartibida keladi, variantlar esa aralash. 6 variantdan 4 tasi kerak — 2 tasi ortiqcha. Har bir savol bo'yicha gapiruvchi odatda bir nechta narsa aytadi: masalan, "History of English" haqida "a bit dull" ham, "clearly sequenced" ham aytiladi — faqat ikkinchisi ro'yxatda bor.

Suhbatdagi fikr o'zgarishi: talaba bir narsani aytadi, tutor to'g'rilaydi ("No — that's an obvious one"). Oxirgi, kelishilgan fikr javob bo'ladi. "But", "though", "whereas", "actually" so'zlaridan keyin diqqatni kuchaytiring.

Short answer: savolga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri javob; NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS — "digital recorders" (2 so'z) to'g'ri, "department's digital recorders" — 3 so'z, xato. Ko'plik kalitda ko'pincha qavs bilan beriladi: mobile phone(s).
presentation: TWO letters da ikkala harfni bitta katakka yozamanmi?
Yo'q. Imtihonda 1 va 2 alohida katak: har biriga bitta harf, tartib ahamiyatsiz (A, D yoki D, A).
Uchala variant ham eshitildi, qaysini tanlayman?
Qaysi biri qabul qilinganini tinglang. "That's a much better idea", "that's also important" — tasdiq; "No", "I wouldn't worry about" — rad.
Matching da bitta harfni ikki marta yozsam bo'ladimi?
Bu turdagi ro'yxatda odatda har harf bir marta. Ko'rsatmani o'qing: "Choose FOUR answers from the box".
Matching savollari tartibdami?
Ha — 5, 6, 7, 8 suhbat tartibida. Variantlar (A–F) tartibda emas.
Kim gapirayotganini qanday bilaman?
Ismlar boshida aytiladi (Amanda, Dr White). Savolda "according to the tutor" bo'lsa, faqat tutor fikri hisobga olinadi.
Short answer da artikl yozamanmi?
Shart emas. "mobile phones" yetarli — "the mobile phones" esa 3 so'z (artikl ham so'z sanaladi) va TWO WORDS chegarasini buzadi.
notes: 5.0 da multiple choice, matching va short answer ni alohida mashq qilgan edik. Endi ular bitta Section 3 da ketma-ket keladi: o'tishda adashmaslik va suhbatdagi FIKRni kuzatish — asosiy ko'nikma.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan tasdiq gapni va tuzoq gapni alohida rangda ko'rsating. TWO letters da uchta noto'g'ri variant nega noto'g'ri ekanini ham so'rang.

Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Workbook audiosini tinglab, 5–8 savollar uchun tutor aytgan har bir baho so'zini (original, backed up, trouble, well put together) yozib olish. Qavsdagi so'zlar — ustoz uchun kalit: o'quvchiga oldindan aytilmaydi (WB — imtihon rejimi).

class_ex.title: Paraphrase ovi: matching variantlari qanday eshitiladi?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz SB 5–8 ro'yxatidagi variantni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar audioda u qanday boshqa so'zlar bilan aytilishi mumkinligini taxmin qiladi.
items: The topic was popular.
It took a long time to write.
It was shorter than the others.
It was well structured.
The content is relevant.
The content is repetitive.
answers: went down well / everyone liked it
I spent ages putting it together
closely linked to / connected with your topic
the same points again and again / too many examples
why: "Go down well" — Section 3 da juda tez-tez keladigan ibora.
Audioda ko'pincha teskari shakl tuzoq bo'ladi: "I didn't take long to put that together".
"Mini-lecture" so'zining o'zi qisqalikni bildiradi.
"Structure" o'rniga "sequenced", "organised", "put together well".
"Relevant" = "related to", "linked to".
"Repetitive" — bir xil narsa qaytarilishi.
class_ex.note: Mashqdan keyin Track 11 ni tinglang va qaysi taxmin to'g'ri chiqqanini tekshiring (masalan, "went down well", "closely linked").

class_ex.title: "Qaysi biri qoldi?" — rad etilgan variant tuzog'i
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar savolga javob beradi va rad etilgan variantni aytadi.
items: "We thought about interviewing teachers, but in the end we went for a questionnaire." — Which method will they use?
"I'd love to use video, but we'll have to make do with audio recordings." — What will they record?
"It's not the length that worries me — it's the lack of examples." — What is the tutor's concern?
"You could use your phones, or we can lend you some cameras if you book them." — Which TWO pieces of equipment?
"The first lecture was long and detailed, whereas this one is quite short." — Which lecture is short?
why: "But in the end" — oxirgi qaror. Interview — rad etilgan.
"I'd love to" — istak, lekin "have to make do with" — haqiqiy tanlov.
"It's not X — it's Y" — Y javob.
Ikkalasi ham taklif qilingan va rad etilmagan — ikkalasi javob (SB 9–10 dagidek).
"Whereas" — qarama-qarshilik: birinchisi uzun, ikkinchisi qisqa.

Beshta variantning ko'pi eshitiladi — qaysi biri qabul qilinib, qaysi biri rad etilganini belgilab boring. Savollar sahifasi quyida rasm sifatida.

tasks.title: Questions 1–4
tasks.type: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: Har savol uchun ikkita harf. Javoblar variantlar tartibida emas, suhbat tartibida keladi.
