tasks.note: Ortiqcha sarlavhalar: iv "Animals that prefer to live alone" (matnda yo'q) va vii "Teaching animals to cooperate" (C dagi tajriba o'rgatish emas, kuzatish — tafsilot tuzog'i).
box: i Sharing a meal to survive
ii What animals gain from friends
iii A change in scientific language
iv Animals that prefer to live alone
v Can we really call it friendship?
viii Partnerships that last for decades

tasks.title: Questions 7–10
tasks.type: Matching features — A–C (harf takrorlanishi mumkin)
tasks.instr: Har gapni ro'yxatdagi to'g'ri variant (A, B yoki C) bilan juftlang. Bitta harfni bir necha marta ishlatish mumkin. Avval variantlarni matnda topib, tagiga chizing.
items: 7 Individuals can identify old companions after a long separation.
8 Some individuals help others that are not part of their family.
9 Stronger relationships were linked to more young surviving.
10 Males work together to achieve a shared aim.
why: "They can recognise the whistle of a former companion even after twenty years apart".
"Including bats that are not relatives".
"Had more infants that survived their first year". "Young" = "infants".
"Males form alliances of two or three individuals that cooperate".

tasks.title: Questions 11–13
tasks.type: Complete the sentences. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
tasks.instr: Gaplar matn tartibida.
items: 11 In the past, scientists described animal friends as 'preferred ___'.
12 A vampire bat may die if it cannot feed for two or three ___.
13 Researchers can record how animals behave but cannot directly see their ___.
why: "Researchers spoke instead of 'preferred partners'".
"An adult that fails to find a meal for two or three nights may starve".
"Scientists can measure behaviour ... but cannot observe feelings directly".

homework_intro: Bugun bitta passage'da uch savol turini birga yechdik: xarita → headings va features belgilari → sentence completion. Uyda xuddi shu tartibda yolg'iz ishlaysiz.

Birinchi vazifa — Practice 3 "Do animals have friends?": 20 daqiqa vaqt oling, 13 savolga javob bering. Har sarlavha yoniga xatboshining asosiy g'oyasini o'zbekcha bir gapda yozing, features variantlarini matnda tagiga chizing.

Ikkinchi vazifa — 30-Day Reading Challenge'dan Day 4 (Questions 1–7 matching headings va Questions 11–13 sentence completion — bu yerda chegara NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS) va Day 29 (Questions 14–20 matching headings va Questions 23–26 matching features). Day 8 va Day 11 ni qilmang — ular bugungi SB va WB matnlari bilan bir xil; Day 17 esa 3-darsda ishlangan. Javoblarni kitob oxiridagi kalit bilan tekshiring.
Uchinchi vazifa — xatolar daftari: bugungi xato javoblarni yozing — savol, to'g'ri javob va sabab ("tafsilotga qarab tanladim", "harfni ikki marta ishlatmadim", "ikki so'z yozdim" va h.k.).

homework.title: Practice 3: "Do animals have friends?"
homework.instr: 20 daqiqada 13 savol; har xatbosh uchun asosiy g'oya bir gapda.
homework.answers: Javoblar Reading bo'limida izoh bilan.

homework.title: 30-Day Reading Challenge: Day 4 va Day 29
homework.instr: Day 4 — Q1–7 (headings) + Q11–13 (sentence completion, NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS); Day 29 — Q14–20 (headings) + Q23–26 (matching features).
homework.answers: Kitob oxiridagi kalit bilan tekshiriladi; ustoz 2 ta sarlavhani isbot bilan so'raydi.

homework.title: Xatolar daftari
homework.instr: Bugungi xato javoblar: savol — to'g'ri javob — xato sababi.
homework.answers: Sababsiz qator qabul qilinmaydi.

kahoot.q: Passage 2 has headings, matching features and sentence completion questions. What should you do first?
options: Look quickly at all three question groups
Write your answers on the answer sheet
kahoot.explain: Avval 1 daqiqada uchala savol guruhini ko'zdan kechirasiz (xarita) — shunda matnda nimani qidirishni bilasiz.

kahoot.q: A correct heading matches a paragraph's…
kahoot.explain: Sarlavha butun xatboshining asosiy g'oyasini beradi, bitta gap yoki tafsilotni emas.

kahoot.q: A paragraph is about world trade and mentions coffee only once. The heading 'Coffee prices' is probably…
kahoot.explain: Bir marta tilga olingan tafsilot sarlavha bo'lolmaydi — asosiy g'oya jahon savdosi.

kahoot.q: There are eight headings for six paragraphs. What does this tell you?
kahoot.explain: Ro'yxatda ortiqcha sarlavhalar bor: har xatboshiga bitta, ikkitasi ishlatilmay qoladi.

kahoot.q: In matching features, are the statements in the same order as the information in the text?
kahoot.explain: Features gaplari matn tartibida kelishi shart emas — shuning uchun variantlarni (ism, tajriba) oldindan matnda tagiga chizasiz.

kahoot.q: The instructions say 'You may use any letter more than once.' What does this mean?
options: One letter may answer several statements
Every letter must be used exactly once
You must write two letters in each box
Each statement has two correct letters
kahoot.explain: Bitta harf bir necha gapga javob bo'lishi, boshqasi esa umuman ishlatilmasligi mumkin — bu normal.

kahoot.q: Matching features: why do you underline EVERY place where a person's name appears?
options: A name may appear in several places
It shows you how many words to write
The names are always in the first line
The first mention is always the answer
kahoot.explain: Bitta odam matnda bir necha joyda uchrashi mumkin — faqat birinchisini belgilasangiz, javobni o'tkazib yuborasiz.

kahoot.q: In sentence completion, the answers come…
kahoot.explain: Sentence completion gaplari matn tartibida keladi — oldingi javob joyidan keyin davom etib qidirasiz.

kahoot.q: ONE WORD ONLY. Text: 'She felt anxious before the interview.' Gap: 'Before the interview, she was ___.' Which answer is correct?
kahoot.explain: Faqat bitta so'z va to'g'ri so'z turi (sifat): 'anxiously' — ravish, 'felt anxious' — ikki so'z.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Text: 'a very close friend'. Gap: 'He shared a flat with a ___.' Which answer gets the mark?
kahoot.explain: 'close friend' — ikki so'z va gapga mos; 'very close friend' — uch so'z, 'a' esa gapda allaqachon bor.

kahoot.q: Your answer is spelt 'relationshp'. The meaning is right. How is it marked?
kahoot.explain: IELTS'da imlo xatosi bo'lsa javob 0 ball — so'zni matndan harfma-harf ko'chiring.

kahoot.q: About how long should you spend on one reading passage in the IELTS exam?
kahoot.explain: 60 daqiqada 3 ta passage — har biriga taxminan 20 daqiqa, javoblarni ko'chirish ham shu vaqt ichida.

kahoot.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'deception'?
kahoot.explain: deception — aldash, aldov; 'trickery' ham shu ma'noda.

kahoot.q: Your siblings are your…
kahoot.explain: sibling — aka-uka yoki opa-singil, ya'ni bir ota-onaning farzandlari.

kahoot.q: 'In the end, he confessed.' This means he…
kahoot.explain: confess — o'z aybini tan olmoq.

kahoot.q: Complete: 'There is strong ___ between the two sisters — each wants to be the best.'
kahoot.explain: rivalry — raqobat: har biri eng yaxshi bo'lishni xohlaydi.

kahoot.q: A child who always gets what they want and behaves badly as a result is…
kahoot.explain: spoilt — erka, ko'p erkalatilgani uchun injiq bo'lib qolgan bola.

kahoot.q: A reliable friend is someone you can…
kahoot.explain: reliable — ishonchli; 'count on' — ishonmoq, tayanmoq.

kahoot.q: 'Her voice gave her away.' What does this mean?
options: It showed what she was hiding
It made her sound confident and relaxed
It was a present from a friend
kahoot.explain: give somebody away — sirini fosh qilmoq: ovozi u yashirayotgan narsani ko'rsatib qo'ydi.

kahoot.q: An acquaintance is someone you…
options: have known and trusted for years
kahoot.explain: acquaintance — tanish: taniysiz, lekin yaqin do'st emas.

lessons.title: Unit 7 Listening — Section 3: Multiple choice + Flow chart
lessons.grammar_topic: Section 3 kombinatsiyasi: Multiple choice (A, B, C) + Flow-chart completion
lessons.vocab_topic: Unit 7 (Relationships) — o'quv loyihasi, taqdimot rejasi, do'stlik tadqiqoti
lessons.book_ref: Complete IELTS Bands 5–6.5: Student's Book, Unit 7, 68–69-betlar (Listening Section 3, CD2 Track 7); Workbook, Unit 7, 42-bet (Listening Section 3, Track 8). Jony Academy mashqi — yangi skript.
objectives: Section 3 da (ikki talaba suhbati) MCQ va flow chart ketma-ket kelganda tayyorlanish vaqtini bo'lish: MCQ — savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oya, flow chart — bo'shliq turi va o'qlar tartibi.
Gapiruvchilarning signal iboralarini ("That's the trouble", "The thing about...", "After that...", "Or better still...") eshitib, javob yaqinlashayotganini sezish.
MCQ tuzog'ini tanish: variantdagi so'z eshitiladi, lekin rad etiladi yoki boshqa narsa haqida aytiladi.
Flow chart'da bosqichlar tartibini kuzatish va gapiruvchi o'z fikrini tuzatganda (places → contexts, changes → influences) oxirgi variantni yozish.
Javobni so'z chegarasi (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS) va imloga rioya qilib transfer qilish.

Jony Academy mashqi skripti — ustoz ikki rolni o'qiydi (yoki kuchli o'quvchi bilan birga).

intro: Section 3 — o'quv mavzusidagi suhbat: odatda ikki talaba (ba'zan ustoz bilan) loyiha, taqdimot yoki tadqiqot haqida gaplashadi. Til Section 1–2 ga qaraganda murakkabroq: fikrlar almashadi, gapiruvchilar bir-birini to'g'rilaydi va rozi bo'lmaydi.

6.0 darajasida Section 3 ko'pincha ikki turdan iborat: Multiple choice (A, B, C) va flow chart (yoki notes) completion. Ular orasida odatda qisqa pauza bo'ladi — o'sha paytda ikkinchi topshiriqni yana bir bor ko'zdan kechiring.

Tayyorlanish vaqtini ikkiga bo'ling. MCQ uchun: savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyaning tagiga chizing ("what PROBLEM", "MUST include", "arrange to") — variantlarga emas (SB 2-mashq). Flow chart uchun: har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligini yozing (ot? ko'plik? joy?) va o'qlar tartibini ko'ring — bosqichlar audioda xuddi shu tartibda keladi.

SIGNAL iboralar javob yaqinlashayotganini bildiradi: "That's the trouble...", "The thing about Mr Dresden is...", "He said that the important thing was...", "The very first thing you need to do is...", "After that...", "The next thing might be...", "Or better still...". Signalni eshitsangiz — keyingi gapga to'liq diqqat.

MCQ TUZOG'I: Section 3 da uchala variant deyarli har doim tilga olinadi. Biri rad etiladi ("Mr Dresden didn't ask for data"), biri boshqa odam yoki boshqa vaqt haqida ("I have to go in the library" — Victor, Fumiko emas). Kim gapiryapti va kim haqida — shuni tekshiring.

FLOW CHART TUZOG'I: gapiruvchi avval bir so'zni aytadi, keyin boshqasi uni to'g'rilaydi yoki yaxshiroq variant taklif qiladi: "places" → "You mean the 'contexts'? — Yes, that's the word"; "future changes" → "or better still, the influences". Oxirgi, kelishilgan so'z — javob.
Transfer: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS — "the animal world" emas, "animal world"; ko'plik -s (key terms, contexts, stages, influences) ko'p ball olib qo'yadi.
formulas: what PROBLEM / MUST include / arrange to
presentation: MCQ da uchala variant ham eshitildi. Qaysi biri?
Savol o'zagiga qayting: KIM haqida va NIMA so'ralyapti? Qolgan ikkitasi odatda rad etilgan yoki boshqa odam haqida.
Flow chart bo'shliqlari ham tartibdami?
Ha. O'qlar bosqichlar ketma-ketligini ko'rsatadi, audio ham shu tartibda boradi.
Gapiruvchi so'zni o'zgartirdi. Qaysi birini yozaman?
Oxirgi, ikkala gapiruvchi rozi bo'lgan so'zni: "Yes, that's the word", "OK, influences".
Signal ibora nima uchun kerak?
U javob yaqinlashayotganini bildiradi. Signalni eshitsangiz, savolni ko'z bilan kuzating va keyingi gapni diqqat bilan tinglang.
"the animal world" deb yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. Bo'shliq oldidan "the" allaqachon bor — faqat "animal world". Artikl ham so'z hisoblanadi.
Bitta javobni o'tkazib yubordim. Nima qilaman?
To'xtamang — keyingi bosqichga o'ting. Oxirida mantiqan eng mos so'zni yozing, bo'sh qoldirmang.
notes: 5.0 da MCQ va flow chart'ni alohida o'rgangan edik. Endi ular bitta Section 3 da ketma-ket — o'rtadagi pauzadan to'g'ri foydalanish asosiy ko'nikma.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan aynan o'sha gapni ekranga chiqaring va signal iborani boshqa rang bilan ko'rsating (SB 3- va 6-mashqlar).
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Workbook audiosidan keyin Maya'ning jadval va diagrammalarini (1 table, 2 tables, pie chart) xotiradan sanab berish.

Grammatika bo'limidagi SB misollari (Tushuntirish kartasidagi tuzoq va transfer misollari, Formulalarning 4–6-bosqich misollari, "the animal world" savol-javobi, Tipik xatolar jadvali) — SB Track 7 javoblarining o'zi. Tushuntirish, Formulalar va Tipik xatolar kartalari proyektor rejimida ham ko'rinadi — grammatika bo'limini Track 7 tekshiruvigacha proyektorga chiqarmang. Doskadagi 10 daqiqalik tushuntirishda strategiyani umumiy misol bilan bering, masalan: rad etilgan variant — "We thought about a poster, but posters are a bit old-fashioned, so let's make a podcast instead" → podcast; o'zini tuzatish — "Then we'll send the forms by post — no, wait, email is quicker" → email; so'z chegarasi — "Bring the ___ to the workshop", eshitiladi "the lab coats" → lab coats ("the" takrorlanmaydi, -s tushmaydi). SB misolini o'sha savolni tekshirganda ko'rsating. Lug'at jadvali ham (sources, key terms, stages, questionnaire misollari) SB va WB javoblarini ochadi — uni WB Track 8 tekshiruvidan keyin oching, aks holda WB imtihon rejimi va uning normativi (10 dan 8) ma'nosini yo'qotadi.
mistakes: C — doesn't know what to focus on

Ma'lumot ko'p: internetda "fascinating reports ... how much has been written"; "I think I've got plenty" esa g'oyalar haqida (Victor: "is it ideas that you need?"). Muammo — mavzuni toraytira olmaslik
"Mr Dresden didn't ask for data" — rad etilgan
Victor to'g'rilaydi, Fumiko "that's the word" deydi

how: CORE — o'quv loyihasi va tadqiqot so'zlari; STRONG — ma'lumotni taqdim etish; SUPER — Section 3 dagi signal iboralar. Ro'yxatni SB va WB tinglangandan keyin ko'rsating: misollar audiodagi gaplarga juda yaqin, oldin ko'rsatilsa javoblarni ochib qo'yadi.
Har o'quvchi o'z loyihasi (maktab yoki kurs) haqida 3 gap aytadi va kamida ikkita yangi so'z ishlatadi.
core: I've got a psychology project this term.
Bu semestr menda psixologiya loyihasi bor.
My tutor gives very broad project titles.
Kuratorim loyihalarga juda keng mavzular beradi.
The project is part of my assessment.
I could do a survey of people of different ages.
Turli yoshdagi odamlar orasida so'rovnoma o'tkazishim mumkin.
Include a list of all your sources.
Start with a definition of your key terms.
Give some background on the topic first.
Avval mavzu haqida umumiy ma'lumot bering.
There are six stages in a friendship.
The subjects couldn't fill in the questionnaire.
She is nervous about her presentation.
strong: A bibliography must be included at the end.
I can't narrow the topic down.
It was only a small sample.
My sample proved to be representative.
My parents have several lifelong friends.
Ota-onamning bir necha umrbod do'sti bor.
I've presented that data in a pie chart.
super: That's the trouble — I don't know where to start.
Text me, or better still, call me.
Menga yozing, yoki undan ham yaxshisi, qo'ng'iroq qiling.
You have to limit the scope of the study.
Tell you what, I'll text you in half an hour.
Mana nima qilamiz, yarim soatdan keyin yozaman.

class_ex.title: Signal iboralar: qaysi savolga? (SB, 3-mashq)
class_ex.instr: Tinglashdan oldin: har signal ibora 1–5-savollardan qaysi biriga javob olib kelishini taxmin qiling. Tinglagandan keyin tekshiring.
items: a The thing about Mr Dresden is ...
b That's the trouble ...
c He said that the important thing was ...
d Look, tell you what, I'll text you ...
e So what reading have you done so far?
why: 2-savol — tutor haqida: "The thing about Mr Dresden is that he likes to find out what you really enjoy working on".
1-savol — muammo: "that's the trouble — I don't really know where to start".
4-savol — loyihada nima bo'lishi SHART: "the important thing was to read about the topic and definitely include a list of all our sources".
5-savol — nima kelishishdi: "I'll text you in half an hour".
3-savol — nima o'qigan: Victor savoli javob yaqinligini bildiradi.
class_ex.note: Kitobda b → 1 namuna sifatida berilgan. Mashqdan keyin doskaga signal iboralar ro'yxatini yozing — dars davomida to'ldirib boriladi.

class_ex.title: Flow chart bo'shliqlarini oldindan aytish (SB, 4-mashq)
class_ex.instr: 6–10-savollarga javob bermasdan, har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z va qanday ma'lumot kerakligini ayting.
items: 6 — "Define ___ using a diagram"
7 — "Background: relationships in the ___, e.g. apes"
8 — "Present an overview of the ___ for human relationships, e.g. work, home"
9 — "Look at six ___ involved in a friendship"
10 — "Predict the future ___ on friendship"
why: "Define" fe'lidan keyin ot — nimani ta'riflaysiz? Loyiha boshida odatda atamalar ta'riflanadi.
"the ___, e.g. apes" — maymunlar misol bo'ladigan soha yoki olam.
"e.g. work, home" — ish va uy — joy yoki vaziyat; ko'plik.
"six ___" — son, demak ko'plik -s.
"future ___ on friendship" — "on" predlogi bilan: effect on / influence on.
class_ex.note: 10-savol uchun o'quvchilar "changes" deyishi mumkin — tinglashda gapiruvchi aynan shu so'zni aytib, keyin to'g'rilaydi. Buni oldindan aytmang, tekshiruvda ko'rsating.

listenings.title: Student's Book, Track 7: Fumiko's psychology project (Q1–10)
intro: Fumiko psixologiya loyihasi haqida Victor bilan gaplashadi; ikkinchi qismda ular birga reja tuzadi. Tinglashdan oldin: 1–5 da savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyani belgilang (SB 2-mashq), 6–10 da bo'shliq turini yozing.
Q1–5 va Q6–10 orasida qisqa pauza bor. Flow chart ko'rsatmasi: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer. Savollar sahifasi quyida rasm sifatida.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Uchala variant ham eshitiladi. Kim haqida va nima so'ralyapti — shuni tekshiring.
items: 1 What problem does Fumiko have with her psychology project? A) She isn't interested in the topic. B) She can't find enough information. C) She doesn't know what to focus on.
2 What point does Victor make about Fumiko's tutor? A) He explores his students' key interests. B) He is a very hard-working member of staff. C) He uses a limited range of project titles.
3 What has Fumiko already read on her topic? A) book extracts B) journal articles C) internet material
4 According to Mr Dresden, Fumiko's project must include A) some graphic data. B) a bibliography. C) a public survey.
5 Victor and Fumiko arrange to A) get in contact in half an hour. B) meet up in the library. C) have lunch together.
why: "That's the trouble — I don't really know where to start ... can't seem to narrow it down". A — tuzoq: "I'm really enjoying it"; B — "I think I've got plenty" g'oyalar haqida, ma'lumot esa ko'p: "there are some fascinating reports".
"The thing about Mr Dresden is that he likes to find out what you really enjoy working on". C — tuzoq: u "broad" (keng) mavzular beradi, cheklangan emas.
"Have you been on the Internet? — I have, and there are some fascinating reports". A — kitoblarni endi olgan, hali o'qimagan; B — jurnal maqolalarini "put them away ... without looking at them".
"Definitely include a list of all our sources" = bibliography. A — tuzoq: "Mr Dresden didn't ask for data"; C — so'rovnoma Fumiko'ning o'z g'oyasi.
"Tell you what, I'll text you in half an hour". B — kutubxonaga Victor yolg'iz boradi; C — kofe va faqat seminar tez tugasa, tushlik emas.
tasks.note: 5-savol yaxshi misol: "library" va "canteen" ikkalasi ham eshitiladi, lekin aniq kelishilgan narsa — yarim soatdan keyin xabar yozish.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Fumiko's plan
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: O'qlar tartibi = suhbat tartibi. Victor Fumiko'ning so'zini to'g'rilaganda yaxshi tinglang.
why: "The very first thing you need to do is give a definition of what you mean by your key terms". "Using a diagram" = "you could just do a diagram".
"You could do a bit of background on the animal world ... relationships among ape groups". "the" formada bor — ikki so'z yoziladi.
Fumiko "places" deydi, Victor: "You mean the 'contexts' for relationships" — "Yes, that's the word". Kalitda — contexts.
"Why don't you go through the stages in a friendship? ... just select six".
"Maybe the future changes in ... — Yeah, or better still, the influences". "changes" — tuzoq.
tasks.note: 8 va 10-savol — Section 3 ning asosiy tuzog'i: birinchi aytilgan so'z emas, tuzatilgan so'z javob.
rows: Background: relationships in the (7), e.g. apes
Present an overview of the (8) for human relationships, e.g. work, home
Look at six (9) involved in a friendship (plus survey)

tasks.title: 6-mashq: signal so'zlar (qayta tinglab)
tasks.type: Bitta so'z yozing
tasks.instr: Track 7 ning ikkinchi qismini qayta tinglang va har signal iboradagi bo'shliqni to'ldiring. Bu iboralar 6–10-javoblardan oldin keladi.
items: 6 I think the very ___ thing you need to do is ...
7 After ___, you could do ...
8 'You mean ... ?' 'Yes, ___ the word.'
9 The ___ thing might be to ...
10 Why don't I ___ by ..., or better still, ...
why: "I think the very first thing you need to do is give a definition..."
"Right. After that, you could do a bit of background..."
"You mean the 'contexts' for relationships. — Yes, that's the word."
"Or the next thing might be to select one type of relationship..."
"Why don't I end by looking into the future? — Yeah, or better still, the influences".
tasks.note: Kitobda bu mashq uchun alohida CD2 Track 8 bor; bu yerda o'sha qism Track 7 dan qayta eshittiriladi.

listenings.title: Student's Book: recording script (CD2 Track 7) — ustoz uchun
intro: Tekshiruvdan keyin ekranga chiqaring. Har javob gapini, signal iborani va tuzoq gapni alohida rang bilan ko'rsating.

listenings.title: Workbook, Track 8: Maya's presentation on lifelong friendships (Q1–10)
listenings.qtype: Multiple choice + Flow chart — imtihon rejimi
intro: Jack va Maya Maya'ning taqdimoti haqida gaplashadi: avval tadqiqot qanday o'tgani (MCQ), keyin taqdimot tuzilishi (flow chart). Avval Workbook 1-mashqini bajaring.
Keyin imtihondagidek: tayyorlanish vaqti, audio BIR MARTA, 10 savol. Flow chart: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.

tasks.title: 1-mashq: 6–10 uchun qanday so'z kerak?
tasks.type: Choose A, B or C
tasks.instr: Tinglashdan oldin flow chart'ni ko'zdan kechiring.
items: 1 What kind of word will be required for all of Questions 6–10? A) adverbs B) verbs C) nouns
why: "change of ___", "Effects of ___", "descriptions of ___", "Changes in ___" — predlogdan keyin ot; 10 esa sarlavha ("___ (e.g. sports, musical tastes)") — ham ot.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Maya har savolda bir nechta narsani aytadi — savol o'zagidagi kalit g'oyaga mos kelganini tanlang.
items: 1 Maya chose the topic of lifelong friendships because A) it was an unusual area of research. B) she had a particular interest in it. C) someone suggested it to her.
2 Maya says that the sample of people she used A) was smaller than she wanted it to be. B) was typical of the population in general. C) was the basis for further work.
3 The problem with the questionnaire was that A) it wasn't well constructed. B) the subjects couldn't engage with it. C) too much time was required to complete it.
4 Maya says that when she conducted the interviews, A) she kept brief notes. B) the subjects were all very relaxed. C) they followed a clear structure.
5 What does Maya say about other research in the area? A) A lot of it contradicted her findings. B) It wasn't very easy to find. C) It was carried out in the same way as hers.
why: "There's been a lot of research on how people form friendships ... but there's not much on this particular topic". B — tuzoq: ota-onasining do'stlari — bu tadqiqot usuli, sabab emas.

"I'd collate the results from that small sample so that I could compare them with more general conclusions from research". A — "small" ni Jack aytadi, Maya norozi emas; B — "representative" keyinroq, taqqoslash natijasi haqida.
"They just couldn't analyse their friendships in that 'cold' way". C — tuzoq: "they hadn't had time" — bahona edi.
"I adapted my questionnaire and sat down with each person" — intervyu anketa asosida, aniq tuzilma bilan. A — tuzoq: yozib olgan, "rather than having to write notes".
"There's not a lot of that, but I managed to locate some academic research". A — tuzoq: "one or two disparities", lekin umuman "confirmed what I found".
tasks.note: 4-savol eng qiyin: "structure" so'zi eshitilmaydi. Anketani moslashtirib, har odam bilan u bo'yicha gaplashgan — shuning uchun intervyu tuzilmali bo'lgan.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Lifelong friendships presentation
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Har bosqichda Maya kategoriya nomini aytadi va qanday ko'rsatganini (table / pie chart) qo'shadi.
why: "The first category I've called 'Change of Location' ... goes to live somewhere else"; "a couple of separate tables" = 2 tables.
"What happens to the friendship when one or both of the friends get married" — "That's a pie chart".
"The next one concerns 'Personality' ... I picked out the most extreme changes".
"How much people had in common in terms of political opinions ... I've constructed another pie chart".
"I've categorised this as 'Shared Interests' ... sports doesn't change ... whereas their musical tastes do".
tasks.note: 7-savolda "married" (fe'l) emas, "marriage" (ot) yoziladi: "Effects of ___" — predlogdan keyin ot. 1-mashqdagi "nouns" javobi shu yerda yordam beradi.
rows: Origins of friendship (age, where began, circumstances, etc.): 1 table
Comparisons between descriptions of (8): patterns of extreme change
(10) (e.g. sports, musical tastes): continuing or changing

listenings.title: Workbook: recording script (Track 8) — ustoz uchun
intro: Skript bilan qayta tinglashda xato qilingan savollarning gapini topishga ishlatiladi. Jack'ning bosqichlarni almashtiruvchi savollarini ("OK, what comes next?", "What then?") belgilang.

listenings.title: Jony Academy mashqi: Friendship project
intro: Ben va Sara — sotsiologiya talabalari — birinchi kurs talabalarining do'st orttirishi haqidagi loyihani rejalashtiradi. Ustoz ikki rolni o'qiydi (yoki kuchli o'quvchi bilan) — oddiy tezlikda (taxminan 150 so'z/daqiqa), rollarni ovoz bilan farqlab. BIR MARTA.
1–5 va 6–10 orasida 20 soniya pauza qiling. Flow chart: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
transcript: BEN: Hi Sara. Have you got a minute to talk about our sociology project?
SARA: Sure, I was going to message you anyway. Have you decided on the focus?
BEN: Well, at first I wanted to look at friendship in general, but Dr Hughes said that was far too wide. So I thought we could look at how first-year students make friends in their first term.
SARA: That sounds manageable. But why first-years?
BEN: Partly because they're easy to find — they're all around us. But mainly because nobody in our department has studied them before. Dr Hughes checked the list of past projects for me.
SARA: Great. And what did he say about the length?

BEN: The written report can be up to three thousand words, but the thing he really stressed was the presentation. It mustn't go over fifteen minutes — he'll stop us if it does. He said he doesn't mind if we don't have many statistics.
SARA: Fifteen minutes isn't much. What about collecting the data? I assumed we'd do an online questionnaire.
BEN: I thought so too, but online surveys get very few replies. My cousin tried one last year and got eleven answers out of two hundred.
SARA: Wow. So what then — interviews?
BEN: Interviews take ages. I think the best option is a short paper questionnaire that we hand out at the start of lectures. Students fill it in on the spot.
SARA: OK. I'm a bit worried about one thing, though. Some students might not want to write about their friends. It's quite personal.
BEN: True. That's why we should make it anonymous — no names at all. And we'll keep it to ten questions, so it's quick.
SARA: And will lecturers let us use their time?
BEN: I've already asked two of them, and they're both happy to give us the first five minutes.
SARA: Perfect. Shall we meet on Thursday to write the questions?
BEN: Thursday's difficult — I've got a seminar all afternoon. How about Wednesday morning, in the café next to the library?
SARA: Wednesday's fine, but that café's always so noisy. Let's book one of the study rooms in the library instead.
BEN: Good idea. I'll book one tonight.
(Pause — 20 seconds)
SARA: Right, let's put the stages in order. What comes first?
BEN: I think the very first thing is to find out what other people have already written. Dr Hughes wants a short literature review — just two or three pages.
SARA: Fine. After that, we write the questions. Should we just use them straight away?
BEN: No — Dr Hughes said we should test them first on a small group. He called it a pilot study.
SARA: Who with? Our flatmates?
BEN: They're second-years, so no. It should be people like our real sample — maybe five first-years from the sports club.
SARA: OK. Then we hand out the questionnaires. We're aiming for two hundred, aren't we?
BEN: Yes. And the next stage is putting all the answers into a spreadsheet. That'll take a while.
SARA: I can do that — I'm quite quick at typing. Then we look for patterns. For example, do students who live in halls make friends faster than students who live at home?
BEN: Exactly — that comparison could be the most interesting part. And we finish with recommendations — what the university could do to help new students. Maybe more social events in the first week?
SARA: Or better still, a buddy scheme, where every new student gets a second-year partner. I think that would help most.
BEN: Agreed. Let's make that our main recommendation.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Uchala variant ham eshitiladi — savol o'zagiga mosini tanlang.
items: 1 What was Ben's MAIN reason for choosing first-year students for the project? A) They are easy to contact. B) No one in the department has researched them. C) The tutor recommended them.
2 What did Dr Hughes say was most important? A) the length of the written report B) keeping the presentation within the time limit C) including a lot of statistics
3 How will the students collect their data? A) an online questionnaire B) interviews C) a paper questionnaire in lectures
4 What is Sara worried about? A) Students may find the topic too personal. B) The questionnaire may be too long. C) Lecturers may refuse to help.
5 Where will Ben and Sara meet to write the questions? A) in a café B) in a library study room C) in the seminar room
why: "Partly because they're easy to find ... But mainly because nobody in our department has studied them before". Savolda MAIN reason so'ralgan: "partly" va "mainly" — asosiy sabab "mainly" dan keyin keladi. A — tuzoq: bu ham sabab, lekin faqat "partly" (qisman); C — tutor mavzuni "far too wide" degan va eski loyihalar ro'yxatini tekshirgan, birinchi kursni tavsiya qilmagan.

"The thing he really stressed was the presentation. It mustn't go over fifteen minutes". A — 3000 so'z tilga olinadi, lekin "but" bilan chetga suriladi; C — "doesn't mind if we don't have many statistics".
"The best option is a short paper questionnaire that we hand out at the start of lectures". A — kam javob; B — "Interviews take ages".
"Some students might not want to write about their friends. It's quite personal". B — Ben aytadi ("ten questions"), Sara xavotiri emas; C — ikki o'qituvchi allaqachon rozi.
"Let's book one of the study rooms in the library instead". A — kafe shovqinli, rad etildi; C — seminar Ben'ning payshanba kungi darsi.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10 — Project stages
tasks.type: Complete the flow chart. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
tasks.instr: Signal iboralarni kuting: "the very first thing", "After that", "the next stage", "Or better still".
why: "Dr Hughes wants a short literature review — just two or three pages".
"We should test them first on a small group. He called it a pilot study". "small group" — tuzoq, bu bosqich nomi emas.
"The next stage is putting all the answers into a spreadsheet".
"Do students who live in halls make friends faster than students who live at home?"
"Maybe more social events ...? — Or better still, a buddy scheme" — "Agreed". "social events" — tuzoq.
tasks.note: 7-savol uchun "flatmates" ham eshitiladi — Ben uni rad etadi ("They're second-years, so no"). 10-savol — SB dagi "or better still" tuzog'ining aynan takrori.
rows: Read previous research and write a short (6)
Write ten questions and test them in a (7) with five first-years
Hand out the questionnaires (target: 200) and enter all answers into a (8)
Look for patterns, e.g. students living in (9) vs students living at home
Recommendations — main one: a (10) for new students

homework_intro: Bugun Section 3 da ikki savol turini ketma-ket yechdik: avval multiple choice, keyin flow chart. Eng ko'p ball ikki joyda yo'qoladi — rad etilgan variantni tanlashda va tuzatilgan so'z o'rniga birinchi eshitilgan so'zni yozishda.

Birinchi vazifa — shadowing: ustoz guruhga SB Track 7 audiosini va skript rasmini yuboradi. Track 7 ning ikkinchi qismini ("Right, so let's design a plan" dan oxirigacha) skript bilan 3 marta tinglang, keyin Victor'ning gaplarini u bilan bir vaqtda takrorlang. Oxirgi urinishni ovozli xabar qilib guruhga yuboring.

Ikkinchi vazifa — diktant: ustoz guruhga WB Track 8 audiosini yuboradi. Uning taqdimot qismini (pauzadan keyin) tinglang va Maya'ning 6 ta gapini to'liq yozing — har bir kategoriya nomi bilan (Change of Location, Personality va h.k.). Diktantni ustoz belgilagan muddatgacha guruhga yuboring; muddat tugagach ustoz skript rasmini yuboradi — solishtiring va xatolarni qizil bilan belgilang.
Uchinchi vazifa — signal iboralar ro'yxati: ikkala audiodan kamida 8 ta signal iborani yozing ("That's the trouble", "After that", "What then?" ...) va har biriga o'z gapingizni tuzing.

homework.title: Shadowing: SB Track 7 (2-qism)
homework.instr: Ustoz guruhga SB Track 7 audiosi va skript rasmini yuboradi. 3 marta tinglash, keyin Victor bilan bir vaqtda takrorlash; ovozli xabar guruhga.
homework.answers: Ustoz talaffuz va ritmni tekshiradi; signal iboralar aniq eshitilishi kerak.

homework.title: Diktant: WB Track 8 (taqdimot qismi)
homework.instr: Ustoz guruhga WB Track 8 audiosini yuboradi. Maya'ning 6 ta gapi to'liq yozilib, muddatgacha guruhga yuboriladi; muddat tugagach, skript rasmi bilan tekshiriladi.
homework.answers: Diktant topshirish muddati tugagach ustoz WB skript rasmini guruhga yuboradi (oldinroq emas); o'quvchi o'zi solishtiradi, xatolarni qizil bilan belgilaydi. Keyingi darsda ustoz 2 ta gapni tasodifiy so'raydi.

homework.title: Signal iboralar ro'yxati
homework.instr: Kamida 8 ta signal ibora + har biriga o'z gapingiz.
homework.answers: Iboralar audiodan bo'lishi shart; o'z gapi yo'q qator qabul qilinmaydi.

kahoot.q: What do you usually hear in IELTS Listening Section 3?
options: One speaker giving a talk on local facilities
A phone call to book a room or a service
A lecture by a professor with no dialogue
kahoot.explain: Section 3 — o'quv mavzusidagi suhbat: 2–3 talaba (ba'zan ustoz bilan) loyiha, taqdimot yoki tadqiqotni muhokama qiladi.

kahoot.q: Section 3 has MCQs (1–5) and a flow chart (6–10). How should you use the preparation time?
options: Mark key words in stems; predict word types for gaps
Read every option in detail and skip the flow chart
Study the flow chart only, as MCQs are easier
Write a guessed answer for all ten questions
kahoot.explain: Vaqtni ikkiga bo'ling: MCQ o'zagidagi kalit g'oya, flow chart'da esa har bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerakligi.

kahoot.q: In a Section 3 multiple-choice question, what should you underline first?
options: the key idea in the question stem
every word in all three options
the names of the two speakers only
the longest of the three options
kahoot.explain: Savol o'zagi nima so'ralayotganini aytadi (what PROBLEM, MUST include); variantlarning esa ikkitasi tuzoq.

kahoot.q: 'I thought about writing on climate, but the reading is very technical — so I've gone for urban gardens.' What is the speaker's topic?
kahoot.explain: Climate tilga olinadi, lekin "but" bilan rad etiladi; yakuniy tanlov — "I've gone for urban gardens".

kahoot.q: An option is mentioned, but it is the OTHER student's plan, not the plan of the person in the question. Is it the answer?
options: No — check who the question is about
Yes — every option you hear is right
Yes — if it is the last thing you hear
Only if both speakers say it twice
kahoot.explain: Section 3 da bir necha odam gapiradi: variant eshitilsa ham, u savoldagi odamga tegishli bo'lishi shart.

kahoot.q: The question asks what the tutor thinks is MOST important. Which phrase signals the answer?
kahoot.explain: "Most", "above all", "the main thing" kabi ta'kid iboralari savoldagi MOST ga mos keladi — javob shundan keyin keladi.

kahoot.q: In a flow-chart completion task, in what order do the answers usually come in the recording?
options: in the same order as the chart
in a random order across the talk
in reverse order, from the end
all together at the very end
kahoot.explain: O'qlar bosqichlar ketma-ketligini ko'rsatadi, audio ham shu tartibda boradi.

kahoot.q: 'Let's end with a short video — or better still, a live demonstration.' 'Yes, much better.' How will they end the talk?
options: with a quiz for the class
kahoot.explain: "Or better still" birinchi g'oyani yaxshirog'i bilan almashtiradi, ikkinchi gapiruvchi ham rozi — javob shu.

kahoot.q: 'The first step is collecting the data — no, sorry, choosing the sample comes first.' What is the first step?
kahoot.explain: Gapiruvchi o'zini tuzatdi ("no, sorry"): birinchi aytilgan so'z tuzoq, tuzatilgani — javob.

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Gap: 'Visit the ___ in week 3.' You hear 'the science museum'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: "the" gapda bor va artikl ham so'z hisoblanadi: "the science museum" uch so'z bo'lib qoladi.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'Interview four ___ of the club.' You hear 'four members' but write 'member'. Is your answer correct?
options: No — the plural -s is needed here
Yes — small spelling slips are fine
Yes — the singular is always accepted
Only if you also write 'the' before it
kahoot.explain: "four" dan keyin ko'plik kerak; -s tushib qolsa, javob noto'g'ri hisoblanadi.

kahoot.q: There is a short pause between Questions 1–5 and 6–10. What is the best use of it?
options: Read the flow chart again and predict
Relax and wait for the next part
Change all your answers to Questions 1–5
Copy your answers onto the answer sheet
kahoot.explain: Pauza — ikkinchi topshiriqni yana bir bor ko'rib, bo'shliqlarni bashorat qilish vaqti; qog'oz imtihonda javoblar varaqaga eng oxirida (10 daqiqada) ko'chiriladi.

kahoot.q: At a British university, what is a 'tutor'?
options: a teacher who guides a small group
a student who lives in the same flat
an office that handles student fees
a person who only marks exams
kahoot.explain: Tutor — kichik guruh yoki alohida talabaga yo'l ko'rsatadigan o'qituvchi (kurator).

kahoot.q: What is a 'questionnaire'?
options: a set of written questions to answer
a spoken interview for a new job
a list of all the books for the course
a table of final test results
kahoot.explain: Questionnaire — anketa: odamlar yozma javob beradigan savollar to'plami.

kahoot.q: Which phrase means 'to do a survey'?
kahoot.explain: "carry out a survey" — so'rovnoma o'tkazmoq; qolgan fe'llar bu ma'noni bermaydi.

kahoot.q: 'The project is part of my assessment.' What does this mean?
options: It counts towards my final mark.
It is just an optional extra task.
It must be done in a group.
kahoot.explain: Assessment — baholash: loyiha natijasi yakuniy bahoga qo'shiladi.

kahoot.q: 'First, give some background on the topic.' What should you give first?
options: basic facts that set the scene
the final conclusions of your study
kahoot.explain: Background — mavzuga kirish uchun umumiy ma'lumot, asos.

kahoot.q: A 'lifelong' friend is someone you have…
options: known for most of your life
worked with for a few weeks
kahoot.explain: Lifelong — umrbod: bolalikdan yoki juda uzoq vaqtdan beri davom etayotgan.

kahoot.q: Which is best for showing how a whole (100%) is divided into parts?
kahoot.explain: Pie chart — doiraviy diagramma: butun (100%) qanday qismlarga bo'linganini ko'rsatadi.

kahoot.q: Which verb goes with 'presentation'? 'She will ___ a presentation on Friday.'
kahoot.explain: "give (make) a presentation" — taqdimot qilmoq; "tell", "say", "speak" bu ot bilan ishlatilmaydi.

intro: Passage 3 — imtihondagi eng qiyin va eng uzun matn: ko'pincha jurnal maqolasi, unda muallifning fikri bor. Unit 8 da uchta savol turi birga keladi: Multiple choice (A, B, C yoki D), YES / NO / NOT GIVEN va Matching sentence endings.

XARITA (1–2 daqiqa). Uchala guruhni ko'zdan kechiring. MCQ odatda matn boshidan oxirigacha tartib bilan boradi va savolning o'zi paragrafni aytadi ("in the first paragraph", "in paragraph 2"). Y/N/NG ham tartib bilan. Sentence endings ham tartibda (Exam advice: "You will find them in the same order"), lekin u matnning ma'lum qismiga — masalan, faqat restavratsiya bosqichlariga — tegishli bo'ladi.

MCQ ning to'rt xili bor: 1) faktik savol ("Zenzie says the project is special because..."); 2) paragraf mavzusi ("What is the main topic of the first paragraph?") — butun paragrafni qamrab olgan variant tanlanadi, bitta gapni emas; 3) muallif maqsadi ("to describe / to explain / to compare") — paragraf NIMA QILAYOTGANINI so'raydi; 4) sarlavha ("most suitable title") — ENG OXIRIDA, subheading va har paragrafning birinchi gapi bo'yicha.

MCQ tuzog'i: variantdagi so'z matnda bor, lekin boshqa ma'noda. Exam advice: "Find the option which expresses the same idea; don't just match words." Har variantni isbot gap bilan tekshiring va nega qolgan uchtasi noto'g'ri ekanini ayting.

YES / NO / NOT GIVEN — T/F/NG ning "egizagi", lekin savol FAKT haqida emas, MUALLIF FIKRI (views / claims) haqida. Muallif fikrini baho so'zlari beradi: in my view, I believe, unfortunately, it is a pity, there's no doubt, too harsh, naive, it isn't hard to see. YES — muallif shunday deydi; NO — muallif teskarisini aytadi; NOT GIVEN — muallif bu haqda hech narsa demaydi (masalan, kelajak haqidagi taxmin, taqqoslash, baho).

Sentence endings: savol boshidagi kalit so'zni (Pictures, A special machine, Nicholas Coleridge, The head of Dior) matnda toping, shu gapni o'qing, keyin tugallanmalar ichidan MA'NOSI mosini tanlang. Tugallanmalar 6 ta, savollar 4 ta — ikkitasi tuzoq. Tugallangan gap grammatik jihatdan ham to'g'ri bo'lishi kerak.
Vaqt: Passage 3 ga 20 daqiqa. Taxminan: xarita 2, MCQ 7, Y/N/NG 5, endings 4, tekshiruv 2. Sarlavha savolini oxirga qoldiring — matnni o'qib bo'lganingizdan keyin u 30 soniyada yechiladi.
formulas: Y/N/NG da muallif baho so'zini toping
unlike, there's no doubt, a pity
Endings: savol boshidagi kalit so'zni toping
presentation: T/F/NG va Y/N/NG ning farqi nima?
T/F/NG — matndagi ma'lumot (fakt). Y/N/NG — muallifning fikri yoki da'vosi. Yechish usuli bir xil, lekin Y/N/NG da baho so'zlariga e'tibor bering.
MCQ da "writer's purpose" savoli nimani so'raydi?
Paragraf nima qilayotganini: tushuntiradimi, solishtiradimi, tasvirlaydimi. Paragrafdagi bitta faktni emas, uning vazifasini tanlang.
Sarlavha savolini qachon ishlayman?
Eng oxirida. Subheading'ni qayta o'qing va har paragrafning birinchi gapini ko'zdan kechiring (Exam advice).
Sentence endings da ikkita tugallanma mos kelyapti.
Matndagi gapni qayta o'qing: qaysi biri aynan shu narsa haqida aytilgan? Ikkinchisi odatda boshqa savolga yoki hech qaysi savolga tegishli emas.
Muallif fikrini aytmasa-chi?
Unda javob NOT GIVEN. Masalan, muallif loyiha 700 soat olishini aytadi, lekin bu reja realmi-yo'qmi — baho bermaydi.
Uchta guruhni qaysi tartibda ishlayman?
Odatda tartib bilan. Faqat sarlavha savoli oxiriga qoladi. Endings uchun kalit so'zlar (ismlar) aniq bo'lsa, ularni oldindan belgilab qo'ying.
notes: 5.0 da MCQ, Y/N/NG va sentence endings alohida o'rganilgan. Bugungi yangilik — ular Passage 3 da birga keladi va vaqt 20 daqiqa.
Har Y/N/NG javobidan keyin so'rang: "Bu fakt yoki muallif fikrimi? Qaysi so'z fikrni bildiradi?"
30-Day Reading Challenge'da Day 9 — Student's Book matni, Day 12 — Workbook matni bilan bir xil. Ularni uyga BERMANG; o'quvchi javobni allaqachon biladi.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: MCQ ning har bir noto'g'ri variantiga "nega noto'g'ri" izohini yozish.
mistakes: Variantdagi so'z matnda bor bo'lgani uchun uni tanlash
Exam advice: don't just match words

Sentence endings da ma'noni emas, so'zni moslash

how: CORE — kiyim va mato haqidagi asosiy so'zlar; STRONG — restavratsiya va dizayn; SUPER — moda sanoati iboralari.
Har so'z bilan o'quvchi o'z kiyimi yoki milliy liboslar haqida bitta gap tuzsin: "My grandmother's atlas dress is very fragile now."

class_ex.title: Fakt yoki fikr?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi. O'quvchilar aytadi: bu FAKT (T/F/NG uchun) yoki MUALLIF FIKRI (Y/N/NG uchun)? Fikrni bildiruvchi so'zni ko'rsating.
items: The dress was first worn on stage in 1888.
It is a pity that so few people know how ikat is made.
The project will need more than 700 hours of work.
In my view, the critics of these repair schemes are too harsh.
Unlike many other actresses of her time, she kept her costumes.
There is no doubt that she would be delighted with the result.
why: Sana — tekshirish mumkin bo'lgan ma'lumot.
"A pity" — muallifning munosabati.
Raqam va reja — fakt; muallif bu reja realmi-yo'qmi demayapti.
"In my view" — fikrning eng aniq belgisi.
Muallif Ellen Terry'ni boshqa aktrisalar bilan solishtiryapti — Y/N/NG savollari ko'pincha shunday gaplarga quriladi (SB 10-savol).
"There is no doubt" — muallif o'z ishonchini bildiradi.
class_ex.note: Mashqdan keyin: Y/N/NG savoli faqat "fikr" gaplardan emas, muallif fakt sifatida da'vo qilgan gaplardan ham tuzilishi mumkin. Asosiy qoida — "muallif shunday deydimi?"

class_ex.title: dress / dresses / clothes / cloth (SB Vocabulary)
class_ex.instr: Har gapga dress, dresses, clothes yoki cloth dan birini qo'ying. Keyin qoidani ayting.

She wore a long silk ___ to the concert.

why: Clothes — har doim ko'plik, umumiy kiyim-kechak (T-shirts, shorts, a jacket — turli kiyimlar).
A dress — sanaladigan: ayollar ko'ylagi.
Cloth — mato, sanalmaydi.
Dress (sanalmaydigan) — kiyinish uslubi: traditional dress, formal dress.
Dresses — bir nechta ko'ylak (evening dresses — kechki ko'ylaklar). "Long ones and short ones" — uzun va kalta ko'ylaklar; clothes (umumiy kiyim-kechak) bunday bo'linmaydi, cloth esa mato.

items: 1 What do you learn about Ellen Terry in the first paragraph? A) Lady Macbeth was her first leading role. B) The Lyceum was her favourite theatre. C) She tried hard to look good on stage. D) She wanted to look young for her audience.

2 What is the writer's purpose in paragraph 2? A) to describe different responses to the Beetlewing dress B) to explain why the Beetlewing dress had such a big impact C) to consider the suitability of the Beetlewing dress for the play D) to compare the look of the Beetlewing dress on and off the stage

3 According to the writer, the main effect of the Lyceum productions was to A) expose more people to Shakespeare's plays. B) reduce the interest in other types of production. C) raise the cost of going to the theatre. D) encourage writers to produce more plays.

4 In the fourth paragraph, what comparison does the writer make between Sargent's portrait and the Beetlewing dress? A) The dress has attracted more attention than the painting. B) The dress is worth more money than the painting. C) The painting took longer to produce. D) The painting looks newer.

5 Zenzie says the Beetlewing project is particularly special because A) the dress is very old. B) people know who wore the dress. C) the dress was designed by someone famous. D) there is evidence that the dress has been used.
6 Which of the following is the most suitable title for the passage? A) A lesson from the past B) A challenging task C) An unusual fashion show D) An unexpected discovery
why: "She knew the power of presentation and carefully cultivated her image." A — Lady Macbeth "a main character", lekin birinchi roli ekani aytilmagan; D — yosh ko'rinish haqida gap yo'q.

Paragraf libosni tasvirlab, uning ta'sirini tushuntiradi va shunday tugaydi: "became one of the most iconic and celebrated costumes of the age". A — tomoshabinlarning "gasp" i 1-paragrafda va bitta reaksiya; D — "no mere stage trickery" sahnadan tashqaridagi ko'rinish bilan solishtirish emas.

"The innovations sold tickets and brought new audiences to see masterpieces that they would not otherwise have seen." Masterpieces = Shakespeare's plays. B — melodramalar ham qo'yilgan, qiziqish kamaygani aytilmagan.
"While the painting remains almost as fresh as the day it was painted, the years have not been so kind to the dress." Rasm yangi ko'rinadi — libos eskirgan.

"It's quite unusual to know who actually wore a garment. That's the thing that makes the Beetlewing project so special." D — tuzoq: "sweat stains and wear marks" har qanday eski kiyimda bor, maxsus sabab emas.
Subheading: "An astonishingly intricate project"; Zenzie: "extraordinarily difficult", "a huge undertaking". C — moda shousi yo'q; D — libos kutilmaganda topilmagan.
tasks.note: 6-savolni oxirida ishlang va subheading'ni qayta o'qing. 5-savolda D ni tanlagan o'quvchiga Zenzie'ning "But" so'zidan keyingi gapini ko'rsating — asosiy fikr "but" dan keyin keladi.

There will be some discussion over the changes that Zenzie's team should make to the dress.

"Zenzie and the National Trust will decide how far back to take the reconstruction, as some members feel that even the most recent changes are now part of the history of the dress." Turli fikr bor — demak muhokama bo'ladi.
Muallif faqat raqamlarni beradi: "more than 700 hours' work". Bu reja realmi-yo'qmi — muallif baho bermaydi.
"Unlike many other actresses, she valued her costumes because she kept and reused them time and time again." "Typical" — "unlike" ning teskarisi.

12 A special machine will be used

why: Tekshiruv "will involve close examination of the dress for signs of damage and wear, and will be aided by comparing it with John Singer Sargent's painting and contemporary photographs". Rasmlar ta'mir qayerda kerakligini aniqlashga yordam beradi.

"The original cloth is quite stretchy, so we've deliberately chosen net because that has a certain amount of flexibility in it too." Stretchy = flexibility — asl matoning xususiyati.
"We'll retain all the evidence on the reverse so that future experts will be able to see exactly what we've done." Reverse = one side.

Scherrer xarajatlarini e'lon qildi "to howls of 'treason' from his colleagues" — hamkasblari g'azablangan. B — boshqalardan yomonroq ahvolda ekani aytilmagan.
"A fair price would have been £50,000, but the couturier could only get £35,000 for it." Adolatli narx balandroq edi. A — teskarisi; C — sotilgan.

"When such a temple of old wealth starts talking about value for money, it isn't to convince anyone that dresses ... are a bargain. Rather, it is to preserve the peculiar mystique..." — ular uchun bu ibora o'zgacha ma'noga ega.

"On one side are those who say that the business will die if it doesn't change. On the other are those who say it will die if it does." Ikkala tomon haute couture qanday omon qolishi — kelajagi haqida bahslashadi. Yakuniy javob: B. D qabul qilinmaydi: matnda "change" so'zi bor, lekin bahs QANDAY o'zgarishlar kerakligi haqida emas — o'zgarish biznesni saqlab qoladimi yoki o'ldiradimi, ya'ni haute couture'ning kelajagi haqida.
tasks.note: 5-savolda ko'p o'quvchi D ni tanlaydi, chunki matnda "change" so'zi bor. Exam advice'ni eslating: so'zni emas, g'oyani moslang. Yakuniy javob — B (the future of haute couture): ikki tomon biznes o'zgarsa yoki o'zgarmasa "will die" deb bahslashadi.

Muallif sababini o'zi tushuntiradi: "Why, then, are the surviving couture houses smiling? Because they trade in fantasy..." Tushunish qiyin emas.

readings.title: Practice 1: Mend and make do — the new culture of repair
readings.qtype: Multiple choice (1–5) + Yes / No / Not Given (6–10) + Sentence endings (11–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi)
text: For most of human history, clothes were far too valuable to throw away. A shirt would be patched when it tore, its collar would be turned when it became worn, and when it could no longer be repaired, the fabric would be cut up to make cleaning cloths or quilts. It was only in the second half of the twentieth century, as mass production made garments cheap, that repair began to disappear from ordinary homes. Today, however, a growing number of people are picking up needles again, and in my view this is one of the most encouraging developments in fashion for decades.

The movement has several sources. Environmental concern is the most obvious. Textile production uses large amounts of water and energy, and much discarded clothing ends up in landfill or is burned. Repairing a garment extends its life, and every extra year of wear reduces the need to make a new one. Yet it would be wrong to see mending simply as an environmental duty. Many of the people who attend repair workshops say that they come for the pleasure of making something with their hands, and for the company of others who share the same interest. Some also point out that a well-repaired garment often fits better than a new one, because it has already taken the shape of its owner.

The style of repair has changed too. Traditional mending aimed to be invisible: a skilled darner could fix a hole in a sock so neatly that it could hardly be seen. Much contemporary mending does the opposite. 'Visible mending' uses contrasting threads, bright patches and decorative stitches to draw attention to the repair. Its supporters argue that a repair is part of a garment's history and should be celebrated rather than hidden. Some of the techniques they use are borrowed from other cultures; Japanese sashiko stitching, which was originally a way of strengthening the clothes of farmers and fishermen, is particularly popular.

Retailers have noticed. Several outdoor clothing companies now offer repair services for their own products, and a few will repair items bought many years earlier free of charge. Cynics suggest that these schemes are mainly a form of marketing, designed to make brands look responsible while they continue to sell more new products than ever. There is some truth in this, but I think the criticism is too harsh: a jacket that is repaired is a jacket that is not replaced, whatever the company's motives may be.

The greatest obstacle to repair is not cost but skill. Sewing was once taught routinely in schools, but in many countries it disappeared from the curriculum decades ago. As a result, many adults today cannot sew on a button, let alone replace a zip. Community repair cafés, where volunteers show visitors how to fix their own clothes and household objects, are trying to fill this gap. Their organisers stress that the aim is not to repair things for people but to teach them to do it themselves, so that they will not need to come back with the same problem.

Design matters as well. Many cheap garments are made in ways that make repair difficult: seams are narrow, fabrics are thin, and some parts are glued rather than sewn. A number of designers are now thinking about repair from the start, for example by using standard buttons and zips that can easily be replaced, or by leaving extra fabric inside the seams so that a garment can be let out if the owner's size changes. Such details add little to the cost of production but can greatly extend a garment's life.

It would be naive to expect mending alone to solve the problems created by the fashion industry. Most people will continue to buy new clothes, and the volume of production is still rising. But the return of repair represents a change in attitude that deserves to be taken seriously. A person who has spent an evening patching a favourite pair of jeans is unlikely to think of clothes as disposable ever again.
glossary: cynic — hamma narsaga shubha bilan qaraydigan odam

the pleasure of making something with their hands, and for the company of others
a jacket that is repaired is a jacket that is not replaced, whatever the company's motives

one of the most encouraging developments
naive to expect mending alone to solve

tasks.title: Questions 1–5
tasks.type: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D
tasks.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D. Savollar matn tartibida; sarlavha savoli (bo'lsa) — eng oxirida ishlanadi.
items: 1 What does the writer say about clothes in the past? A) They were usually made at home. B) They lasted longer because fabrics were stronger. C) They were reused in different ways until they were worn out. D) They were more fashionable than clothes today.

2 According to the second paragraph, many people who attend repair workshops A) are mainly worried about the environment. B) enjoy the practical and social side of the activity. C) want to save money on new clothes. D) learned to sew at school.

3 What is the main difference between traditional and visible mending? A) Visible mending is quicker. B) Visible mending uses only Japanese techniques. C) Traditional mending needed special tools. D) Traditional mending tried to hide the repair.

4 What is the writer's opinion of company repair schemes? A) They are useful whatever the reason for them. B) They are simply a way of selling more clothes. C) They should be free for every customer. D) They are too expensive for most people.
5 What is the main purpose of repair cafés? A) to repair items cheaply for visitors B) to sell second-hand clothes C) to help people learn to repair things themselves D) to train professional tailors
why: "A shirt would be patched ... its collar would be turned ... the fabric would be cut up to make cleaning cloths or quilts." A va B — matnda yo'q.
"They come for the pleasure of making something with their hands, and for the company of others." A — tuzoq: muallif "it would be wrong to see mending simply as an environmental duty" deydi.
"Traditional mending aimed to be invisible"; visible mending "draw[s] attention to the repair". B — tuzoq: sashiko faqat misol ("some of the techniques").
"I think the criticism is too harsh: a jacket that is repaired is a jacket that is not replaced, whatever the company's motives may be." B — bu tanqidchilarning fikri, muallifniki emas.
"The aim is not to repair things for people but to teach them to do it themselves." A — aynan inkor qilingan.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10
tasks.type: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN
tasks.instr: YES — gap muallifning fikriga mos keladi; NO — muallifning fikriga zid; NOT GIVEN — muallif bu haqda nima deb o'ylashini aytib bo'lmaydi.

why: "In my view this is one of the most encouraging developments in fashion for decades."
"It would be wrong to see mending simply as an environmental duty" — boshqa sabablar ham bor.
Muallif ikki uslubni tasvirlaydi, lekin qaysi biri ko'proq ommalashishi haqida taxmin qilmaydi.
"There is some truth in this" — muallif tanqidchilarni qisman to'g'ri deb biladi. "Completely wrong" — zid.
"It would be naive to expect mending alone to solve the problems created by the fashion industry."

readings.title: Practice 2: Ikat — the cloud-tied cloth of Central Asia
readings.qtype: Multiple choice (1–5) + Yes / No / Not Given (6–10) + Sentence endings (11–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi)
text: Few textiles are as instantly recognisable as ikat. Its bold patterns, in which one colour seems to melt into the next, can be found on cushions, bags and dresses in shops around the world. Yet many of the people who buy these products have no idea how the original fabric is made, or that one of its great historic centres lies in the Fergana Valley of Uzbekistan. In my view, this lack of awareness is a pity, because the story behind the cloth is at least as remarkable as its appearance.

The name ikat comes from a Malay word meaning 'to tie', and it describes the key stage of the process. Before any weaving takes place, bundles of thread are stretched out and tightly bound in certain places so that dye cannot reach them. The bundles are then dyed, the bindings are removed, and the process is repeated for each new colour. Because the dye always spreads a little under the bindings, the edges of the pattern are never perfectly sharp. This slight blurring, which a machine would treat as a fault, is exactly what gives ikat its character.

In Central Asia the technique is known as abrbandi, from a Persian word for 'cloud' — a reference to the soft, cloud-like edges of the designs. Traditionally, different specialists were responsible for each stage of production. One person designed the pattern and tied the threads, another prepared the dyes, and a third did the weaving. Dyeing with indigo was often carried out by a separate group of craftsmen who worked only with that colour. A single length of fine cloth could therefore pass through many pairs of hands before it was finished. The patterns themselves carried meaning. Some designs are said to represent natural forms such as pomegranates, tulips or rams' horns, while others were believed to protect the wearer from harm. Because each workshop developed its own variations, experienced buyers could often tell where a piece of cloth had been made simply by looking at it.

Two main types of fabric were produced. Khan-atlas is made entirely of silk and has a smooth, shining surface, while adras combines silk with cotton, which makes it heavier and more hard-wearing. In the nineteenth century, robes made from these fabrics were worn by wealthy people as a sign of their status, and they were also given as gifts on important occasions such as weddings.

During the twentieth century, much production moved into large factories, and many traditional skills were in danger of being lost. Factory ikat was cheaper, but the designs became simpler, synthetic dyes replaced natural ones and the quality of the cloth declined. It was only towards the end of the century that a serious revival began, as craftspeople in Margilan and elsewhere reopened small workshops, relearned older techniques and began to train apprentices. Today visitors can watch the whole process, from the unwinding of silk cocoons to the finished cloth.

International interest has brought both opportunities and problems. Fashion designers in Europe and America have repeatedly used ikat patterns in their collections, and this has helped to create new markets for hand-woven fabrics. Designers from Uzbekistan itself have also begun to present ikat garments at international fashion events. However, much of what is sold as 'ikat' in Western shops is in fact printed, with the pattern simply copied onto the surface of ordinary cloth. Such products are not dishonest in themselves, but I believe customers deserve to be told clearly what they are buying.

The future of the craft will depend on whether it can remain both authentic and profitable. Some weavers have started to experiment with new colours and lighter fabrics that suit modern tastes, and a few now sell directly to customers online. Purists object that this is a betrayal of tradition. I do not share this view: traditions have always changed, and a craft that refuses to adapt is more likely to die than one that welcomes new ideas.
glossary: purist — an'anaga qat'iy amal qilishni talab qiladigan odam
paraphrases: have no idea how the original fabric is made
an essential part of its appeal
exactly what gives ikat its character
different specialists were responsible for each stage
contains cotton as well as silk
lost some of its traditional qualities
designs became simpler ... quality of the cloth declined
this lack of awareness is a pity
customers deserve to be told clearly
purists object that this is a betrayal of tradition

readings.title: Practice 3 (uyga): Fast fashion — counting the cost
readings.qtype: Multiple choice (1–5) + Yes / No / Not Given (6–10) + Sentence endings (11–14)
readings.source: Jony Academy — yangi matn (Passage 3 darajasi), uy vazifasi
text: Over the past three decades, the way people buy clothes has changed dramatically. Large retailers now introduce new designs not twice a year, as was once the norm, but every few weeks, and prices have fallen so low that a T-shirt can cost less than a sandwich. This model, known as 'fast fashion', has made fashionable clothing available to almost everyone. It has also, I would argue, encouraged us to treat clothes as if they were disposable.

The speed of the system depends on close links between design and production. When a new style appears on a catwalk or is worn by a celebrity, designers working for fast-fashion brands can produce a similar garment and have it in shops within a few weeks. Sales figures are checked daily, so that popular items can be reordered quickly and unpopular ones withdrawn. From a business point of view, the system is remarkably efficient: it greatly reduces the risk of producing large quantities of clothes that nobody wants to buy. Some companies first produce small trial batches of a new design and place larger orders only once they see how well it sells.

The environmental costs, however, are considerable. Growing cotton requires large amounts of water and, in many regions, pesticides. Synthetic fibres such as polyester are made from oil, and when they are washed, they release tiny plastic fibres that can end up in rivers and seas. Estimates of the industry's total contribution to global carbon emissions vary widely, and some of the figures quoted in the media are, in my opinion, unreliable. Nevertheless, there is no serious doubt that the overall impact is large.

Social concerns have also been raised. Much clothing is produced in countries where wages are low and working conditions can be poor. A number of major brands have introduced codes of conduct for their suppliers, and some publish lists of the factories they use. Critics argue, however, that such measures are hard to enforce, because production is often passed on to smaller workshops that are rarely inspected.

The low price of fast fashion also affects how long clothes are kept. Many garments are worn only a handful of times before being thrown away or pushed to the back of a wardrobe. When clothes cost so little, there is little reason to look after them carefully or to have them repaired, and a small fault such as a broken zip can be enough to end a garment's life.

Consumers are often blamed for the situation, but this seems to me only partly fair. Surveys suggest that many shoppers say they care about how their clothes are made, yet continue to choose the cheapest option. This gap between attitudes and behaviour is not simply hypocrisy: it can be very difficult for an ordinary shopper to find reliable information about a garment's origins. Labels usually state only the country where it was finally put together, not where the cotton was grown or the fabric was woven.

Several alternatives to fast fashion are now being tested. Clothing rental services allow customers to wear an outfit for a special occasion and then return it. Second-hand clothing, once associated mainly with charity shops, is now bought and sold in large quantities online. Some brands have begun to collect used garments in their stores, promising to recycle them. Recycling textiles, however, is technically difficult, particularly when fabrics are made from a mixture of fibres, and only a small proportion of the clothing collected is actually turned into new fibre.

Ultimately, the most effective change may also be the simplest: buying fewer clothes and wearing them for longer. This does not mean giving up an interest in fashion. On the contrary, choosing a smaller number of well-made garments and combining them in different ways requires more thought about style, not less. It also means paying more attention to how clothes are washed and stored, since good care can add years to a garment's life.
paraphrases: encouraged us to treat clothes as if they were disposable
avoids producing too many unwanted clothes
reduces the risk of producing large quantities of clothes that nobody wants
the country where the garment was finally made
the country where it was finally put together
requires more thought about style, not less

kahoot.q: Passage 3 has multiple choice, YES/NO/NOT GIVEN and sentence endings. What should you do in the first two minutes?
options: Map which part of the text each group covers
Read the whole passage slowly from start to end
Answer the sentence endings before anything else
Look up every unknown word in the passage
kahoot.explain: Avval xarita: 1–2 daqiqada har savol guruhi matnning qaysi qismiga tegishli ekanini belgilab olamiz, keyin tartib bilan ishlaymiz.

kahoot.q: In a Passage 3 multiple-choice group, which task is usually best left until the end?
kahoot.explain: Sarlavha savoli butun matnni so'raydi — uni oxirida, subheading va har paragrafning birinchi gapini qayta ko'zdan kechirib ishlaymiz.

kahoot.q: A question asks: 'What is the writer's purpose in paragraph 3?' What are you looking for?
options: What the whole paragraph is doing
One fact from the paragraph's first line
The opinion of an expert who is quoted
The meaning of a difficult word there
kahoot.explain: Purpose savoli paragraf NIMA QILAYOTGANINI (tushuntiradi, solishtiradi, tasvirlaydi) so'raydi, undagi bitta faktni emas.

kahoot.q: A paragraph describes old factories that became hotels, shops and schools. What is its main topic?
kahoot.explain: Mavzu savolida butun paragrafni qamrab olgan variant tanlanadi; bitta misol (hotel yoki shop) mavzu emas.

kahoot.q: A multiple-choice option repeats three words from the passage. What should you do?
options: Check if it expresses the same idea
Choose it, because the words match
Reject it, because it copies the text
Choose it only if it is the longest
kahoot.explain: Exam advice: don't just match words — so'z matnda bo'lsa ham, variant o'sha g'oyani aytayotganini isbot gap bilan tekshiramiz.

kahoot.q: How is YES/NO/NOT GIVEN different from TRUE/FALSE/NOT GIVEN?
options: It tests the writer's views and claims
It tests only numbers and dates
It never has a NOT GIVEN answer
It is only about the last paragraph
kahoot.explain: Y/N/NG muallifning fikri yoki da'vosini tekshiradi, T/F/NG esa matndagi faktni; yechish tartibi o'xshash.

kahoot.q: Text: 'In my view, the new museum is far too small for its collection.' Statement: 'The museum needs more space.'
options: YES – 'too small' means it needs room
NO – the writer thinks the museum is fine
NOT GIVEN – no size is mentioned
NOT GIVEN – this is only a fact
kahoot.explain: "In my view" — muallif fikri; "far too small for its collection" = ko'proq joy kerak, demak YES.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Many people believe handmade toys are safer, but there is little evidence for this.' Statement: 'Handmade toys are proven to be safer.'
options: NO – there is little evidence for it
YES – many people believe they are safer
NOT GIVEN – toys are not compared
NOT GIVEN – the writer gives no view
kahoot.explain: Boshqalarning fikri muallifning fikri emas: muallif "little evidence" deydi, "proven" esa bunga zid — NO.

kahoot.q: Text: 'The bridge took ten years to build and now carries 5,000 cars a day.' Statement: 'The bridge will need repairs soon.'
options: NOT GIVEN – no view on its future
NO – it is used every day
YES – busy bridges always need repairs
NO – it took ten years to build
kahoot.explain: Muallif ko'prikning kelajagi haqida hech narsa demaydi — javob NOT GIVEN; o'z bilimimiz bilan taxmin qilmaymiz.

kahoot.q: Text: 'In my opinion, most online reviews are useful.' Statement: 'Online reviews are always useful.'
options: YES – the writer likes online reviews
NOT GIVEN – reviews are not described
kahoot.explain: "Always" — mutlaq so'z: muallif faqat "most" deydi, shuning uchun gap uning fikriga zid — NO.

kahoot.q: There are six sentence endings (A–F) for four questions. What does this mean?
options: Two endings will not be used
Each ending can be used twice
kahoot.explain: Ikkita tugallanma ortiqcha (tuzoq): har savolga bitta tugallanma, har tugallanma ko'pi bilan bir marta.

kahoot.q: In sentence endings, how do you find the right place in the passage?
options: Use the key words at the start of each question
Search the passage for the words in each ending
Start from the end of the passage and go back
Look for the longest paragraph in the text
kahoot.explain: Savol boshidagi kalit so'z (ism yoki narsa) matnda tez topiladi; savollar matn tartibida keladi.

kahoot.q: Sentence start: 'The new traffic rules ___'. Which ending fits grammatically?
options: have reduced accidents in the city.
has reduced accidents in the city.
to reduce all accidents in the city.
kahoot.explain: "The new traffic rules" — ko'plikdagi ega, shuning uchun "have reduced"; tugallangan gap grammatik jihatdan ham to'g'ri bo'lishi kerak.

kahoot.q: She bought two metres of blue ___ to make a skirt.
kahoot.explain: Cloth — mato (sanalmaydi): two metres of cloth; clothes esa tayyor kiyim-kechak.

kahoot.q: 'The old manuscript is very fragile.' This means it…
options: is worth a lot of money
kahoot.explain: fragile — mo'rt, nozik: oson shikastlanadi, ehtiyot bo'lib ushlash kerak.

kahoot.q: Experts plan to ___ the old mosque to its original condition.
kahoot.explain: restore — tiklamoq, restavratsiya qilmoq: binoni asl holatiga qaytarish.

kahoot.q: Leather boots are very ___: a good pair can last for twenty years.
kahoot.explain: durable — chidamli: uzoq vaqt buzilmaydi; fragile esa teskari ma'noda.

kahoot.q: 'The wedding was extravagant.' This means it was…
options: small and quiet with few guests
kahoot.explain: extravagant — dabdabali, isrofli: keragidan ortiq pul sarflangan.

kahoot.q: A building design that 'stands the test of time'…
kahoot.sub: Lug'at: stand the test of time
options: is tested before it is built
wins a prize in a competition
kahoot.explain: stand the test of time — vaqt sinovidan o'tmoq: ko'p yillar o'tsa ham qadri tushmaydi.

kahoot.q: 'Haute couture' describes clothes that are…
options: made by hand for individual clients
made in factories in standard sizes
kahoot.explain: haute couture — yuqori moda: har bir mijoz uchun qo'lda tikiladigan eksklyuziv kiyim.

intro: Section 4 — imtihonning oxirgi qismi: bitta ma'ruzachi akademik mavzuda gapiradi (tarix, fan, dizayn). Boshqa section'lardan farqi — o'rtada PAUZA YO'Q: 10 savolni oldindan o'qib olasiz va audio oxirigacha to'xtamaydi.
Eng ko'p uchraydigan savol turi — sentence completion yoki note completion. Bugungi ikkala kitob mashqida ham: "Complete the sentences below. Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer."

TAYYORLANISH (45 soniya). Har gapda: 1) kalit so'zni tagiga chizing (sashiko means, in the beginning, warm fabrics, workers such as...); 2) bo'shliqqa qanday so'z kerak — ot, ko'plikdagi ot, sifat, nom, sana; 3) gapning boshidagi vaqt belgisi (In the past, In the 1930s, Nowadays) — ma'ruza tartibini ko'rsatadi.

PARAPHRASE: savoldagi so'z audioda boshqacha aytiladi — "means" = "translates as", "not needed" = "no longer necessary", "old clothes" = "ancient garments". Lekin JAVOBNING O'ZI audiodagi aynan so'z bo'ladi (Exam advice: "You will hear the exact word(s) you need").

SIGNAL SO'ZLAR ma'ruzada yangi qism boshlanganini bildiradi: "Now, what does that word mean?", "So the point here is...", "Then, in 1895...", "Now, there are exhibitions...". Bitta savolni o'tkazib yuborsangiz, signal so'zni kutib, keyingi savolga o'ting.

TUZOQLAR: ma'ruzachi bo'shliqqa mos keladigan bir necha so'z aytadi. Masalan, gap "The building was ___ rather than modern" bo'lsa, ma'ruzachi "modern" so'zini ham aytadi, lekin javob uning teskarisi (masalan, "traditional"). Savoldagi so'z bo'shliq ichida takrorlanmaydi.
TRANSFER: so'z chegarasi (TWO WORDS — "silk scarves" bo'ladi, "silk scarves for winter" bo'lmaydi), imlo, ko'plik -s. Gapni javob bilan birga o'qing — grammatik jihatdan to'g'rimi?
formulas: vaqt belgilari: In the past, In the 1930s
means, warm fabrics, workers such as
Now... / So the point here is...
presentation: Section 4 da pauza bo'lmasa, qachon o'qiyman?
Audio boshlanishidan oldin berilgan vaqtda (odatda 45 soniya) — 10 savolning hammasini o'qing.
Javobni o'z so'zim bilan yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. Javob audiodagi aynan so'z. Paraphrase faqat savol gapida bo'ladi.
"Firemen" yoki "fire men" — qaysi biri to'g'ri?
Kalitda ikkalasi qabul qilinadi. Lekin imlo xatosi ("firemans") — 0 ball.
Ikkita javob eshitdim, qaysini yozaman?
Gapning qolgan qismiga mos kelganini: "rather than decorative" — demak, bo'shliqda "decorative" ning teskarisi.
"Many layers" yozsam bo'ladimi yoki faqat "layers"?
Ikkalasi ham to'g'ri — ikki so'z chegarasi ichida. Kalitda: layers / many layers.
Bitta savolni o'tkazib yubordim.
To'xtamang. Keyingi savol kalit so'zini tinglang; oxirida bo'sh joyga mantiqiy taxmin yozing.
notes: 5.0 da Section 4 va note completion alohida o'rganilgan. 6.0 da asosiy qiyinchilik — uzun ma'ruzada (7–8 daqiqa) pauzasiz 10 savolni kuzatish va paraphrase'ni tez tanish.
Tekshiruvda har javobdan keyin skriptdan aynan o'sha gapni ko'rsating va savoldagi paraphrase juftligini doskaga yozing.
Kuchli o'quvchilarga: Workbook audiosini skriptsiz ikkinchi marta tinglab, har savol oldidan kelgan signal so'zni yozib chiqish.

Proyektor rejimida "Tushuntirish", "Formulalar" va "Tipik xatolar" ning ikki ustuni o'quvchilarga ko'rinadi — ularda SB/WB javoblari yo'q, misollar umumiy ("The building was ___ rather than modern", "silk scarves"). SB/WB javoblari faqat ustozga ko'rinadigan joylarda: "Tipik xatolar" ning 3-ustuni va "Firemen yoki fire men", "Ikkita javob eshitdim", "Many layers" savol-javoblari. Doskadagi 12 daqiqalik tushuntirishda ularni aytmang, o'sha savolni tekshirganda ko'rsating — aks holda WB imtihon rejimi va uning normativi (10 dan 8) ma'nosini yo'qotadi.
mistakes: "rather than X" bo'shlig'iga eshitilgan X ni yozish
SB 2-savol: "decorative" yozish xato — gapda "rather than decorative", teskarisi kerak; javob "functional".
Gapdagi shartga (warm, not available) mos so'zni yozish
SB 3-savol: "asa" yoki "cloth" yozish xato — asa mahalliy, issiq bo'lmagan mato; javob "wool".
Joy belgisini (In the towns) e'tiborsiz qoldirish
SB 6-savol: "country people" yozish xato — ular qishloqda; gapda "In the towns" — javob "firemen / fire men".
WB 4-savol: "Levi" yozish xato — keyin o'zgartirilgan ism (tuzoq); javob "Leob" (L-E-O-B).
Gapda bor so'zlarni ham javobga qo'shib yozish
SB 4-savol: "many layers of material" — 4 so'z, "of material" gapda bor, chegara buziladi; javob "layers / many layers".

how: CORE — tikish va mato so'zlari; STRONG — kiyim tarixi va ma'ruza tili; SUPER — ma'ruzachi iboralari.
Har o'quvchi milliy kiyim (chopon, atlas ko'ylak, do'ppi) haqida 3 gaplik mini-ma'ruza tuzadi va 3 ta so'zni ishlatadi.
Takrorlash (L16 da o'tilgan, bu darsda yangi so'z sifatida sanalmaydi): stitch — chok; tikmoq. Uning o'rniga CORE ro'yxatida yangi so'z — seam.
